items.author: Jose Antonio Lanz
items.content:
In brief
- Elon Musk said Tuesday that SpaceX and Tesla have each formed special committees of independent directors to study a merger, though no terms have been agreed.
- A combined company worth roughly $3.5 trillion would own the Grok chatbot, X, Starlink, the Terafab chip project, the Starmind orbital data center plan, and Tesla's robotaxi and Optimus businesses.
- Any deal needs the backing of 50% of all outstanding Tesla shares, which Musk called "quite a high hurdle," and Tesla's annual meeting is set for December 3.
Elon Musk said Tuesday that the boards of SpaceX and Tesla have each formed special committees to study merging his two biggest companies, a deal that would put rockets, electric cars, humanoid robots, a social network and the Grok chatbot inside a single corporation worth roughly $3.5 trillion.
“I do think there’s a lot of merit to combining the companies as we are pretty much in the superintelligence singularity,” Musk said on SpaceX’s third-quarter earnings call. The singularity is Silicon Valley shorthand for the point where AI outsmarts humans and starts improving itself faster than anyone can keep up.
He then listed what the two companies would share: “superintelligence software, chip design, the Terafab obviously, robotics, mass-to-orbit with the Starmind constellation, connectivity.”
In plain English, that means AI models, custom chips, a giant chip factory, robots, and satellites that work as data centers in orbit.
If it happens, one company—with one man holding the majority of its votes—would own a leading AI chatbot, the social network that feeds it data, the satellites that connect it, the factory that makes its chips, and the cars and robots it is meant to drive.
Nothing has been signed and Musk warned that assuming a merger is a certainty “would be overstating it.” If you own an S&P 500 index fund, you already hold a sliver of Tesla—not SpaceX—and in an all-stock deal those shares would likely be swapped for stock in the combined company.
It would be Musk’s third consolidation since March 2025, when xAI absorbed X (formerly Twitter). In February, SpaceX swallowed xAI in a deal valuing the AI company at $250 billion, weeks after Tesla put about $2 billion into it; in June, SpaceX went public in the largest IPO ever.
SpaceX reported third-quarter revenue of $14.58 billion on Tuesday, well above the $12.72 billion analysts expected. It also booked its first quarterly profit since going public, largely by renting the computing power of its AI server farms to firms such as Anthropic and Google.
The most ambitious piece is Starmind, SpaceX’s plan to put AI data centers in orbit. The company has asked U.S. regulators to approve up to 1 million satellites that would run AI models on near-constant sunlight, and Musk expects deployments to start in late 2027 and reach “significant scale” in 2028.
Musk’s argument is that Earth is running out of room and electricity for AI, and the politics back him up. An Annenberg survey found 61% of Americans now oppose new data centers in their area, and roughly $130 billion in projects were blocked or delayed in the first quarter of 2026 alone.
SpaceX’s own IPO paperwork, however, warned investors that orbital AI computing relies on “unproven technologies” and “may not achieve commercial viability.” Tesla’s main contribution would be Terafab, a $16.8 billion chip factory the two companies are building in Texas to supply Optimus robots, Cybercab robotaxis, and those space data centers.
Musk isn't the first to look past dry land to keep servers cool. Microsoft's Project Natick sank 855 servers off the coast of Scotland in 2018. Over two years only six failed, a 0.7% rate against 5.9% for a comparable group on land, yet Microsoft shut the program down anyway, with cloud operations chief Noelle Walsh saying, “I’m not building subsea data centers anywhere in the world.”
China has since picked up the idea with a wind-powered underwater data center about six miles off Shanghai, which its builder, HiCloud, says uses at least 30% less electricity than land-based rivals, while startup Lonestar aimed at launching a small data storage unit toward the Moon in early 2025.
Wall Street mostly likes the idea, at the right price. “We believe this is a no-brainer move for both SpaceX and Tesla, it comes down to the price for shareholders,” Dan Ives of Yorkville Ives & Co. told Reuters, estimating Tesla shares would need to be valued around $550 apiece—a premium, or bonus over the market price, big enough to win the vote.
Tesla spiked almost 4% after Elon’s statements went public. His words were more powerful for Tesla’s stocks than building a flying car, considering the stock dipped after the demonstration.
Even if nothing is for certain, markets are flirting with the idea. Tesla investor Gene Munster of Deepwater Asset Management now puts the odds of a deal within two years at 95%.
SpaceX is also a major contractor for the U.S. military, intelligence agencies, and NASA, while Tesla relies heavily on its Shanghai factory, a national security mix Reuters said could draw scrutiny from both Washington and Beijing.
A merger would also hand Musk the tighter grip on Tesla he has long demanded. He owns about 20% of Tesla but controls most of SpaceX’s votes through supervoting shares—stock that carries extra votes—and Barclays estimates he would hold about 56% of the votes in a combined company.
SpaceX reacted much more favorably with a 10% spike, the best movement since June.
Any deal still needs the support of 50% of all outstanding Tesla shares, not just those cast, a bar Musk called “quite a high hurdle.” Barclays suggested last week that an announcement could come before Tesla’s annual meeting on December 3.

Cardano Foundation urges EU against expanding MiCA rules to DeFi and staking
The foundation called for regulation based on financial risks rather than technology, warning that overlapping rules could create uncertainty for crypto businesses across the EU.
The Cardano Foundation has urged the European Union not to introduce new, standalone regulations for decentralized finance and staking, arguing that existing financial laws should govern such activities based on their functions and risks rather than the technologies they use.
In a Wednesday blog post outlining its 19-page Sept. 30 submission to the European Commission, the foundation called for a distinction between direct participation in decentralized networks and financial services provided by intermediaries, particularly those involving custody or control of users’ assets.
“Regulation should follow the substance of an activity, the functions performed, and the risks created, not the technology through which it is conducted,” the foundation wrote.
The foundation said Cardano users can delegate their native ADA (ADA) tokens to help secure the network without surrendering custody or locking their tokens, arguing that such participation should be treated differently from staking services operated by intermediaries.
The submission also called for clearer distinctions between the EU’s Markets in Crypto Assets Regulation (MiCA) and existing financial laws, warning that overlapping requirements and inconsistent interpretations across member states could create uncertainty for crypto businesses.
The foundation’s position comes as EU regulators consider expanding oversight of crypto services. In September, the European Securities and Markets Authority (ESMA) recommended additional safeguards for staking, lending and borrowing, along with a new regulated service category for firms providing access to DeFi protocols.
The Cardano Foundation has also pushed for greater regulatory clarity across the Atlantic, joining five other blockchain organizations in an Oct. 20 letter urging the US Securities and Exchange Commission to formally recognize digital commodities as non-securities under its proposed crypto framework.

items.author: Aaron Wise
items.content:
A bug that allows hackers to remotely execute code has been discovered in PHP, the language that powers 70% of the world’s websites.
PHP shipped emergency fixes today for two of the most critical flaws, but over one-third of the web remains unpatched as of publication time.
The language, used to program website backends, runs on servers, not in the browser, and sends its resulting HTML or other dynamic data to the browser.
Official fixed releases only cover PHP 8.2 and newer, leaving over one-third of PHP websites without a patch.
Mid-day, backports were starting to roll out across older versions 7.4-8.1. Unfortunately, according to one estimate, more than 800,000 internet hosts serving content to millions of websites run a branch of PHP so old “that will get no fix” at all.
The two flaws, CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619, are collectively PHP2Shell.
PHP2Shell lets an unauthenticated attacker run code on a web server and serve buggy outputs to a user’s browser.
Hackers’ exploits can occur even before a website’s own code executes.
Read more: Whitehat hacker accuses Injective of ghosting after $500M bug disclosure
AI hacked PHP, found a bug affecting most websites
A security researcher using OpenAI’s GPT-5.6 Sol model discovered the bug during an August audit funded by OpenAI.
That researcher was part of Calif, a partner in OpenAI’s Patch the Planet program, which pairs frontier models with expert human cybersecurity review.
The bug class had been flagged decades earlier yet dismissed as too hard to exploit, Calif’s CEO Thai Duong told the Wall Street Journal.
However, AI hackers have now figured out how to seize control of a server’s memory within a few dozen requests.
Wiz, a division of Google Cloud, confirmed the flaws independently. Wiz’s co-founder called PHP2Shell “the most severe AI vulnerability that was ever found,” and one humans would probably never have found.
Cloudflare reacts as PHP alarms ring around the world
Cloudflare’s CTO Dane Knecht reported live exploit vectors for every customer, including free plans.
The website cacheing giant implemented a stopgap emergency measure overnight before announcing more patches a few hours later.
The PHP bug had worldwide impact. Finland’s state IT center shut several government web services as a precaution.
Meanwhile, in the Netherlands, NotuBiz’s council information sites for local governments went offline, with MijnOverheid and the Dutch parliament’s site following.
Patched versions of PHP include 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36, and 8.2.35. However, 27% of PHP sites still run PHP 7, and 7.7% run PHP 5, which remain unpatched.
GoDaddy urged customers to upgrade.

items.author: Jose Antonio Lanz
items.content:
In brief
- Bitcoin trades near $84,500, up 2.5% in 24 hours, as the crypto market cap rose 2.6% to $2.82 trillion; XRP gained 4.1% and Zcash 11.2%.
- Brent crude near $108 and a 5.09% 10-year Treasury yield drove October's selloff, and both eased slightly on Wednesday.
- Bitcoin technical indicators still suggest caution, but prediction markets lean optimistically bullish.
Bitcoin traders and hodlers are breathing this week after a pretty spooky start to the month with the historically best gains.
Bitcoin traded near $84,500 on Wednesday, up 2.5% over 24 hours, as the crypto market bounced back from a mid-October slide that pushed it below $80,000. The total crypto market capitalization, the combined value of every coin, rose 2.2% to $2.9 trillion.
Ethereum climbed 2.5% to $2,504, Solana gained 2.2% to $108.18 and BNB rose 2% to $749. XRP led the large caps with a 4.1% gain to $1.37, while Zcash jumped 11.2% to $1,332 and has now added 15.3% over seven days.
The Crypto Fear & Greed Index, a 0-to-100 gauge where 0 means extreme fear and 100 means extreme greed, reads 55, which counts as neutral but is 3 points ahead of yesterday’s readings. In other words, it seems like traders have stopped panicking, but they are not yet chasing prices.
Brent crude, the global oil benchmark, has swung between $97 and $112 a barrel this month and traded near $108 on Wednesday. The war with Iran keeps supply fears alive, and Washington rejected an Iranian plan to reopen the Strait of Hormuz in late September.
Oil matters to crypto because it feeds inflation. U.S. consumer prices rose 3.7% in September from a year earlier, above the 3.6% economists expected and up from 3.4% in August. Higher inflation pushes up Treasury yields, the annual return investors demand for lending to the U.S. government. Government bonds paying more than 5% with almost no default risk pull money away from stocks and crypto, and higher rates make the borrowing behind leveraged trades costlier.
The Federal Reserve's benchmark rate sits at 3.75% to 4% after a September hike, and CME FedWatch gives about an eight-in-ten chance of a hold at the Oct. 28 meeting. Markets firmly expect a hike on Dec. 9.
Bitcoin price: Going up, but weak
On the daily chart, Bitcoin opened Wednesday at $82,928.80 and has reached $84,726.28, up 1.94% for the candle, after bouncing about 6% from this month's low near $79,711. Its current price is pressing up, trying to approach the natural resistance at $87,422.70.
Bitcoin’s latest rally ran from $62,763 to a September high of $87,422.70. That trend marked a strong support at $81,603. Bitcoin lost the level in the October dip and has now reclaimed it, with movement still in the upper side of its bounce..
The 50-day exponential moving average, an average of recent closing prices that gives more weight to the most recent days, sits near $80,782, above the 200-day moving average at about $76,084. A 50-day above the 200-day is the standard sign of an uptrend, and Bitcoin trades 4.6% above the shorter average.
The Relative Strength Index, or RSI, which scores recent buying against selling on a 0-to-100 scale, reads 58.5. Readings above 50 mean buyers hold the edge, while 70 marks overbought territory, so momentum is not yet stretched but is moving towards a bullish mood.
The bullish scenario needs a daily close above $84,726, today's high, ideally with ADX—an indicator of a trend’s strength over time—climbing back above 25 to confirm a trend. That would open a natural target at around $86,090, and then the September high at $87,422.70.
Traders on Myriad, a prediction market built by Decrypt's parent company Dastan, put the odds of Bitcoin touching $87,500 in October at 31%, down from 45% on Oct. 12. A $90,000 touch is priced at 18%.
A stall below $84,726 would keep Bitcoin inside the roughly $79,700 to $87,400 range that has held since late September, which fits an ADX under 20.
The bearish case starts with a daily close below $81,603. That would expose the 50-day EMA at $80,782, then the October low near $79,711, and the 200-day EMA at $76,084.

items.content:
UK financial watchdog opens consultations for DeFi guidance, crypto laws
The UK Financial Conduct Authority consultations came just weeks after the agency opened applications for companies under its new crypto regulatory regime.
The UK’s Financial Conduct Authority (FCA) announced two consultation periods for how companies using decentralized finance can comply with its guidance, and exclusions for certain crypto assets following “recent legislative changes.”
In a Wednesday notice, the FCA opened consultation periods for helping DeFi companies comply with the financial watchdog’s rules on money laundering and financial crime. The agency also announced a consultation for “exclusions from cryptoasset regulation,” citing recent legislation in the country.
Regarding DeFi, the FCA said that the proposed guidance “seeks to clarify existing rules rather than establish new policy.”
“DeFi sits among the most innovative parts of [Financial Services],” said the UK Cryptoasset Business Council in response to the consultations. “The UK can still strike the right balance - clear perimeter rules, expectations that stay proportionate, and a framework that lets responsible innovation take root here instead of migrating elsewhere [...] the FCA needs to get this right.”
The crypto regulation exclusions referred to the FCA’s reveal of a regulatory regime, including stablecoin holding arrangements and reserve assets, expected to be enforced starting in October 2027. The FCA opened applications for crypto entities on Sept. 30, with a Feb. 28, 2027 deadline for companies seeking to be in compliance with the rules.
Related: UK sanctions three crypto exchanges tied to Russian illicit funds
items.title: UK financial watchdog opens consultations for DeFi guidance, crypto laws

⚡️互联网基础软件一日内接连曝出安全风险，涉及PHP、Node.js与Go

BlockBeats 消息，10 月 22 日，多个互联网基础软件项目一日内接连发布安全更新，涉及远程代码执行、TLS 证书校验绕过及证书信任风险。其中：

PHP 修复 CVE-2026-109618、CVE-2026-109619 两项严重漏洞，均可导致未经身份验证的远程代码执行，影响处理 Web 请求的 PHP 环境。修复版本包括 8.5.12、8.4.27、8.3.36 和 8.2.35。

Node.js 公告列出十项漏洞，其中四项为高危，包括 Brotli 解码器越界写入导致的远程代码执行、DNS 名称截断，以及两项 TLS 证书主机名校验绕过问题。修复版本为 26.12.1、24.22.1 和 22.23.4。

此外，Go 的 crypto/x509 相关风险编号为 CVE-2026-111943，Red Hat 将其评级为「重要」，CVSS 3.1 评分为 6.8。攻击者在具备特定网络位置及相关证书等条件下，可能冒充合法服务器，拦截或篡改通信。Go 1.26.10 和 1.27.3 已加入拒绝列表，阻断对相关失陷中间证书的信任。

items.author: Cointelegraph by Sam Bourgi
items.content:
Treasury Secretary Bessent likens GENIUS Act to Lincoln-era banking reform
The OCC has finalized rules for stablecoin reserves and redemptions, with Bessent calling the GENIUS Act a “watershed moment for American finance.”
US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent has compared the Trump administration’s landmark stablecoin legislation to banking reforms enacted under President Abraham Lincoln, drawing parallels between two efforts to establish a national framework for American currency more than 160 years apart.
In a Wednesday post on X, Bessent hailed the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency’s (OCC) final rule implementing the GENIUS Act, calling the legislation a “watershed moment in American finance.”
Bessent drew a comparison to the National Currency Act of 1863, which established a federal framework for nationally chartered banks to issue currency. He argued that the GENIUS Act serves a similar purpose for payment stablecoins in the digital age.
Bessent said the OCC rule would support “private-sector innovation, competition, and American leadership in digital assets.”
Source: Scott Bessent
As Cointelegraph reported Wednesday, the OCC finalized rules governing stablecoin reserves, redemptions and related services. The rules are scheduled to take effect on Jan. 18, 2027.
Jonathan Gould, comptroller of the currency, described the regulations as a “clear, practical framework for payment stablecoin innovation.”
Related: Mastercard launches stablecoin risk screening for banks and payment providers
What the OCC’s stablecoin rules mean for issuers
The GENIUS Act, signed into law in 2025, established a federal regulatory framework for payment stablecoins. The OCC’s final rule sets out how that framework will apply to issuers under its supervision, including requirements for reserves, redemptions and risk management.
Beginning Jan. 18, 2027, companies issuing payment stablecoins in the United States will generally need regulatory approval under the GENIUS Act. Issuing stablecoins without the required authorization could carry penalties.
The OCC said the final rule covers national banks, federal savings associations, federal branches of foreign banks and nonbank companies seeking approval to issue payment stablecoins under federal supervision. It also covers certain foreign payment stablecoin issuers.
The rules come as dollar-denominated stablecoins gain traction for payments and money transfers, even as growth in their overall supply has stalled.
Related: Stablecoin remittances cost 84% less than traditional transfers, report finds
items.title: Treasury Secretary Bessent likens GENIUS Act to Lincoln-era banking reform

⚡️PHP漏洞应对：网站运营方需立即更新版本，普通用户应加强账号安全与防钓鱼保护

BlockBeats 消息，10 月 22 日，据 PHP 官方安全公告，针对「php2shell」漏洞，网站运营方应按所用分支更新至 PHP 8.5.12、8.4.27、8.3.36 或 8.2.35，或安装发行版提供的对应修复包。PHP 8.1 及更早版本用户，应升级至受支持分支，或联系发行版及长期支持厂商确认旧版本补丁。

普通用户可参考 CISA 的通用安全建议：一是在邮箱、金融账户等重要账户启用双因素认证；二是为不同账户设置独立强密码，避免密码复用；三是警惕冒充「紧急密码重置通知」的钓鱼邮件，需要改密时自行打开官网或官方 App 操作，避免点击可疑链接。上述措施有助于降低盗号及钓鱼风险，但不能修复服务器端 PHP 漏洞。

Cloudflare 提醒，漏洞位于服务器的 PHP 运行环境，仅更新网站代码或插件无法修复。使用托管服务的用户应联系服务商确认底层 PHP 已更新。Cloudflare 宣布，为 Web 应用防火墙（WAF）新增完整 HTTP 事务检测及响应规则，面向包括免费套餐在内的所有客户开放。修复期间应保持 WAF 防护开启，但 WAF、上传限制等措施不能替代补丁。

网络安全公司 Huntress 建议，企业全面盘点服务器、控制面板及第三方软件中的 PHP 环境，优先修复公网系统；无法及时修复的停服维护版本，应考虑暂时隔离公网访问。同时监测 PHP 进程异常启动命令行、解释器或下载工具等行为，发现可疑活动后隔离服务器，并保留网站及 PHP 日志。

原文链接 https://m.theblockbeats.info/flash/373056

items.content:
In brief
- Dogecoin Labs launched together with the Dogecoin Foundation, consolidating the meme coin’s scattered products, IP, and development teams.
- Led by CEO Jordan Jefferson, it aims to close the gap between Dogecoin’s massive community and its thin lineup of real apps.
- It builds on recent groundwork: DogeOS’s Sept. 30 testnet and MyDoge’s 500,000-plus users.
Dogecoin is getting a dedicated company to build out its ecosystem, as the teams behind the meme coin’s biggest consumer products fold into a single organization aimed at giving DOGE more everyday uses.
Announced Tuesday, Dogecoin Labs was formed together with the Dogecoin Foundation to consolidate the products, intellectual property, and development teams scattered across the Dogecoin world into one independent outfit.
It will own and operate three flagship products: the MyDoge wallet, the DogeOS app platform, and Such App, a merchant-payments tool, with assets and talent contributed by both the Foundation and House of Doge.
The pitch is to close a gap the company sees as Dogecoin’s defining weakness. Despite ranking among the largest and most recognizable cryptocurrencies, with deep liquidity, millions of holders and one of crypto’s most active communities, the number of actual products and businesses built on DOGE remains small relative to that audience. Dogecoin Labs, led by CEO Jordan Jefferson, the founder of MyDoge and DogeOS, intends to change that by building wallets, payments, commerce, trading, DeFi, gaming, AI and social apps.
“No other digital asset has Dogecoin’s combination of liquidity, community and cultural reach, and its potential has barely been tapped,” Jefferson said, adding that the community has chanted “DOGE to $1” for years and that the goal now is “to build the economy that ambition calls for.”
The move builds on recent groundwork. DogeOS opened its public testnet on Sept. 30, giving developers an Ethereum-compatible environment to build Dogecoin apps, while MyDoge, which grew past 500,000 users without paid acquisition, rolled out a V3 update connecting the wallet to those applications. Together with Such App’s merchant rails, the three products are meant to link developers, consumers and businesses into a functioning DOGE economy.
The Foundation will continue its stewardship, open-source support and advocacy while Labs handles commercial product development.
The reorganization arrives during a soft stretch for the token. DOGE traded around $0.084 on Tuesday, up 3.9% on the day for a roughly $13 billion market cap, but down about 14% over the past month and off roughly 88% from its May 2021 record.
Dogecoin’s institutional story has been mixed, too: a Dogecoin Foundation-backed 21Shares DOGE ETF launched on Nasdaq this year, though Bitwise later shut its own Dogecoin fund citing low demand and a need to “optimize its product range to meet evolving investor needs.”

items.author: Jacob Lyon
items.content:
Italian police have busted a mafia-linked crypto laundering ring that moved €68 million ($76 million) out of the country under the guise of a Milan-based car rental company.
According to Il Sole 24 Ore, the operation, carried out by the Guardia di Finanza and Monza Brianza, has seen 30 individuals arrested and stretches across Italy, Spain, and Switzerland.
The scheme allegedly took funds from drug trafficking, crypto scams, fraudulent invoices, and general bank accounts, combined them, and moved them into European banks.
Crypto exchanges were then used to convert the funds sending them onto wallets controlled by the suspects.
A Milan-based car rental run by suspects with ties to the Ndrangheta and Camorra mafia groups was reportedly central to the plot. These suspects are alleged to have used their profits to support mafia members in prison.
Members of one of Italy’s youngest mafia groups, the so-caled “Fourth Mafia,” were also reportedly involved.
Shell companies generated false invoices
Various shell companies used €110 million ($123 million) worth of false invoices, generated for businesses that never involved contracted work, to launder the funds before they were converted into crypto.
Read more: Europol raids $24 million ‘mafia crypto bank’
The scheme attracted crypto scammers, drug traffickers, and tax evaders looking to launder their funds, and police are looking to make seizures totaling €21 million ($23.5 million).
Two individuals, including a Milan magistrates office driver, and a Milan-based lawyer, have also been arrested.
Just last week, Bank of America was fined $1.2 billion for failing to detect $5 billion worth of suspicious transactions that include funds linked to Chinese money laundering networks.
American Express was also fined $350 million this month for allegedly processing billions of dollars in trade-based money laundering.

BlockBeats 消息，10 月 22 日，Node.js 项目于 10 月 21 日发布安全更新，涉及 26.x、24.x 和 22.x 版本分支，修复版本分别为 26.12.1、24.22.1 及 22.23.4。本次公告共列出 10 项漏洞，包括 4 项高危、3 项中危和 3 项低危，各版本分支的受影响范围有所不同。

其中，高危漏洞 CVE-2026-111497 涉及 Brotli 解码器越界写入，可导致远程代码执行，影响上述三个版本分支。其他高危问题包括 DNS 解析中的空字符处理，以及 TLS 证书主机名验证绕过。

本次更新还修复了持久连接响应处理、随机数缓存重复及权限模型等问题，并更新 c-ares、OpenSSL、Undici 等依赖组件。官方提醒，已终止支持的版本同样可能受安全漏洞影响，用户应使用受支持的最新版本。

此前报道，PHP 修复了两项可导致未经身份验证的远程代码执行的严重漏洞，修复版本为 8.5.12、8.4.27、8.3.36 和 8.2.35，官方敦促用户立即升级。

items.author: Decrypt Staff
items.content:
In brief
- Elon Musk’s floated SpaceX-Tesla merger would unite the companies’ combined 30,221 BTC, worth roughly $2.5 billion, into one of the largest non-mining corporate Bitcoin treasuries.
- SpaceX’s stash was effectively invisible to public markets until its June IPO filing, having quietly accumulated for years.
- Musk cautioned a deal isn’t “a certainty,” and neither company has signaled buying or selling.
Elon Musk’s floated merger of SpaceX and Tesla would do more than unite rockets and electric cars. It would fold two of the world’s largest corporate Bitcoin stashes onto a single balance sheet.
Speaking on SpaceX’s third-quarter earnings call Tuesday, Musk said the boards of both companies had formed special committees of independent directors to weigh a tie-up, cautioning that treating a deal as “a certainty” would be “overstating it.”
But the prospect alone has drawn fresh attention to the combined entity’s crypto holdings.
Tesla reported 11,509 BTC in its most recent quarterly filing, while SpaceX disclosed 18,712 BTC in the S-1 it filed ahead of its June IPO. Together, that’s 30,221 BTC, worth roughly $2.5 billion at Bitcoin’s recent price near $83,000.
As Decrypt reported when the merger idea first surfaced, combining the two would stack one of the largest non-mining corporate Bitcoin positions anywhere under Musk’s control, placing the merged company among the top handful of public holders, trailing only the likes of Michael Saylor’s Strategy and a few others.
The SpaceX portion is the more striking piece. The rocket maker’s 18,712 BTC was effectively invisible to public markets until its IPO filing, meaning a substantial treasury had quietly accumulated inside a private company for years before anyone could count it, more than double what blockchain trackers had previously attributed to SpaceX wallets. The combined cost basis across both firms sits around $1 billion, implying an average buy price near $35,000 per coin.
A merger wouldn’t change anything about Bitcoin itself, and neither company has signaled plans to buy or sell. Both have held their positions static, with SpaceX last moving coins in prior years and Tesla reporting no changes.
What a deal would alter is governance and accounting: one of the most closely watched corporate Bitcoin piles would sit inside a single public vehicle, subject to quarterly disclosures and the fair-value accounting that recently forced Tesla to book a loss as Bitcoin slid.
For now, the treasury math is hypothetical, living or dying with a transaction that remains exploratory. But it underscores how, almost incidentally, a Musk mega-merger would also create a Bitcoin giant.

items.content:
Chainlink, Cardano, other blockchain groups push SEC for clearer crypto rules
Six major blockchain organizations urged the SEC to formally recognize digital commodities as non-securities in its proposed regulatory framework.
Six major blockchain organizations, including Chainlink Labs and the Cardano Foundation, have urged the US Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) to formally classify digital commodities as non-securities, as the agency’s public consultation on proposed crypto regulations came to a close Tuesday.
In a joint letter dated Oct. 20, Chainlink Labs, the Cardano Foundation, Hedera, Aptos Labs, Ava Labs and the Stellar Development Foundation called on the SEC to incorporate its digital commodity classification directly into the proposed Regulation Crypto Assets framework, arguing that interpretive guidance alone leaves market participants facing legal uncertainty.
The groups argued that the SEC’s existing interpretation recognizes digital commodities as a distinct category but that the proposed rules fail to explicitly reflect that distinction, potentially leaving developers and other market participants uncertain about which securities regulations apply.
Source: Taylor Barr
The letter also seeks greater clarity on how securities laws apply to secondary-market transactions involving digital assets, as well as the treatment of staking and other activities associated with decentralized blockchain networks.
The SEC’s proposed crypto framework, introduced in August, drew roughly 140 public comments over 60 days, with industry participants and legal scholars offering competing views on proposed exemptions for crypto offerings and a conditional safe harbor for certain tokens.
items.title: Chainlink, Cardano, other blockchain groups push SEC for clearer crypto rules

items.author: Jake Harrison
items.content:
Abracadabra DAO, the DeFi project behind the long-depegged Magic Internet Money (MIM) stablecoin, has passed a controversial proposal to wind down the protocol on its second attempt after reducing quorum requirements from 3 billion to 300 million SPELL, worth just $26,000.
The proposed “orderly wind down” came less than four months after the DAO passed a “strategic transition of stewardship,” promising to “revitalize Abracadabra… and establish a clear roadmap for the long-term success of SPELL and the broader Abracadabra platform.”
Following a period in which the stewardship team claims it “worked effortlessly” to turn things around, an attempt to shut down the once-$6 billion protocol, in late September, proved controversial.
It put the “actionable backing” of MIM’s 22 million supply at just $900,000 and proposed a resolution for MIM holders of four cents on the dollar.
What wasn’t mentioned, however, were the unexplained outflows worth almost $9 million in June and July. But the proposal was keen to point out the “risk of facing users enforcing a liquidation via legal actions, which is more costly to all stakeholders.”
Read more: Abracadabra blames hacks for shutdown amid ‘looting’ claims
Last week’s “refined” vote was identical apart from a lower quorum threshold, and was pushed over its newly-defined line thanks to votes cast directly from an address labelled “Abracadabra.Money: MIM Treasury” on Etherscan.
No mention has been made of the $3 million worth of WETH that the address has accumulated in recent days, either, nor whether that sum will be added to the “effective backing” of MIM.
Read more: Magic Internet Money loses its sparkle as DeFi platform hacked for $6.5M
Quorum quibbling
Just two voters participated in the latest Snapshot vote, the first run of which was branded “treasury looting,” but ultimately failed to pass quorum with just over 100 million SPELL votes in total.
One of these addresses, the proposal’s author, cast 100 million SPELL votes in favour.
Of these, 40 million were bought with USDC received directly from the MIM treasury-labelled wallet and a further 59.5 million were bought with WETH, the majority of which also came from the treasury wallet. The other 296 million votes were cast by the treasury wallet itself.
Keen eyed readers will notice that the 396 million votes also fall well short of the 3 billion SPELL quorum set for Abracadabra DAO votes.
The “refined” proposal contains a “quorum adjustment disclosure,” stating that, with just over 1 billion SPELL supply at time of publishing the proposal, “the current quorum is therefore totally irrelevant and needs to be adjusted… [to avoid] paralysing the protocol.”
However, with the Snapshot space’s admin keys held by previous Abracadabra team members who are “not reachable,” the space’s “hardcoded quorum cannot be fixed.”
Citing “simplicity” and users’ “best interests” the proposal states that a new quorum will be set at 30% vote participation, “in line with market standards.”
The vote, despite Snapshot displaying it as “rejected,” is apparently passed, according to the terms set out in the quorum adjustment disclosure.
Protos has reached out to Jack Niewold, named as Project Lead in the June proposal, but hadn’t received a response at the time of publication.

items.author: Decrypt Agent
items.content:
In brief
- Bitcoin-backed loans let holders pledge BTC as collateral to borrow dollars or stablecoins, keeping exposure to Bitcoin's price and often avoiding a taxable sale.
- Loan-to-value ratios typically run from about 30% to 70%, and borrowers face margin calls or liquidation if Bitcoin's price falls sharply.
- The market has matured since the 2022 lender collapses, with an investment-grade securitization and big banks joining in, though published rates still run from about 5.8% to 14%.
Most long-term Bitcoin holders know this problem. You need cash for a house deposit, a business or a tax bill, but selling BTC means giving up exposure to its future price. In many countries it also means paying capital gains tax. A Bitcoin-backed loan is a way around that: you pledge your Bitcoin as collateral and borrow dollars or stablecoins against it.
The idea is as old as lending itself. People have long borrowed against homes, stock portfolios and gold. What's new is the collateral, an asset that trades around the clock and can swing in price by double digits in a week.
The market collapsed in 2022, when lenders including Celsius and BlockFi went bankrupt. It has since come back in a more cautious form, with centralized lending more than tripling from its late-2023 low, according to Galaxy Research.
This guide covers what Bitcoin-backed loans are, how they work, who offers them, and the risks borrowers should understand before taking one out.
What is a Bitcoin-backed loan?
A Bitcoin-backed loan is a secured loan with BTC as the collateral. You deposit Bitcoin with a lender, or lock it in a smart contract. In return you get a loan worth a fraction of that Bitcoin's value, paid in fiat currency such as U.S. dollars or in a stablecoin such as USDC.
While the loan is open, your Bitcoin stays locked. Once you repay the principal plus interest, you get it back.
Lenders lean on the collateral rather than your income history, so many of these loans need little or no traditional credit check. They come in two broad types:
- Centralized (CeFi) loans, from companies such as Ledn, Strike, Unchained, Nexo and Coinbase. You go through identity checks, and the company or its custodian holds your BTC.
- Decentralized (DeFi) loans, from protocols such as Aave and Morpho. A smart contract holds the collateral, and native BTC usually has to be "wrapped" into a token on another blockchain first.
Did you know?
Wrapped Bitcoin is a token on another blockchain, such as Ethereum, that is backed 1:1 by real BTC held in custody. It enables Bitcoin to be used in DeFi apps.
How does a Bitcoin-backed loan work?
The key number is the loan-to-value (LTV) ratio: how much you borrow compared with the value of your collateral. Industry LTVs typically range from about 30% to 70%, and many lenders start at 50%. At a 50% LTV, $100,000 of Bitcoin gets you a $50,000 loan.
That cushion matters because Bitcoin is volatile. If BTC's price falls, your LTV rises. Lenders set thresholds:
- Margin call: if your LTV rises past a set level, you're asked to add more collateral or repay part of the loan.
- Liquidation: if the LTV keeps rising, the lender sells some or all of your Bitcoin to cover the debt. In DeFi, smart contracts do this automatically.
Terms vary. Some products have fixed 12-month terms with monthly interest. Others, such as Coinbase's loans, have no monthly payments and no repayment deadline. Interest simply builds up on the balance.
Did you know?
"Rehypothecation" means a lender re-lends your collateral to someone else to earn extra yield. It was a big reason customers of failed lenders in 2022 lost their deposits.
What's so special about Bitcoin-backed loans?
The main draw is getting cash while keeping your Bitcoin. In many jurisdictions, borrowing is not a taxable event, but selling is. Check your local rules, though.
The sector has also matured. Lenders now advertise that they don't rehypothecate collateral, and some offer "collaborative custody." Unchained, for example, keeps loan collateral in a 2-of-3 multisig vault: the borrower, Unchained and an independent key agent each hold one key, and no single party can move the coins alone.
Wall Street is paying attention too. In February 2026, Ledn closed a $188 million Bitcoin-backed asset-backed securitization. S&P Global assigned its $160 million senior class a preliminary "BBB-" rating, which SVB described as the first investment-grade rating for a Bitcoin-collateralized lending portfolio. Galaxy put total crypto-backed loan volume at $56.16 billion in Q2 2026, down 16.8% from the previous quarter as borrowers cut back on leverage, with centralized lenders now holding more loans than DeFi protocols.
Did you know?
Coinbase has passed $1 billion in Bitcoin-backed loan originations, according to the company.
Who's offering Bitcoin-backed loans?
- 🏦 Ledn: a Bitcoin-focused lender with custodied loans whose collateral isn't lent out.
- 🔐 Unchained: commercial loans held in multisig vaults where the borrower holds a key.
- ⚡ Strike: Bitcoin-backed loans for individuals and businesses in select U.S. states.
- 🔵 Coinbase: on-chain loans run through the Morpho protocol, available in most U.S. states.
- 💳 Aven: launched a Bitcoin-backed Visa credit line in April 2026 with limits up to $1 million.
- 🌐 Nexo: instant credit lines against BTC and 100+ other assets, mainly for non-U.S. users.
- 🧮 Aave: a DeFi lending protocol where you can borrow against wrapped BTC.
What does a Bitcoin-backed loan cost?
Rates depend on loan size, LTV and provider, and they change often. As of October 2026, published rates start at about 5.8% at Coinbase. SALT advertises 7.49% to 10.5% APR, while Ledn's rates run from 11.49% APR on loans below $250,000 down to 9.25% on loans of $2 million or more. Strike charges between 10.5% and 13% APR on loans with monthly interest payments, and a percentage point more if interest is paid at maturity. Unchained quotes a 12% interest rate, or 14.18% APR. DeFi rates float with supply and demand. Lower LTVs and bigger loans usually get better rates.
Also look for origination fees, prepayment penalties and liquidation fees. These can push the effective cost well above the headline rate.
How to get a Bitcoin-backed loan
- Pick a provider. Compare custody model, rehypothecation policy, rates and where it operates.
- Complete KYC. Centralized lenders require identity verification.
- Choose your LTV and term. A conservative LTV leaves more room before a margin call.
- Deposit BTC into the lender's custody, a multisig vault or a smart contract.
- Receive funds in fiat or stablecoins, then watch your LTV and repay to unlock your Bitcoin.
The future of Bitcoin-backed loans
Bitcoin lending is starting to look like ordinary finance. Regulation is clearer after the GENIUS Act passed in the U.S., and the administration is friendly to crypto, although the broader CLARITY Act stalled in the Senate in September 2026. SVB notes that several major financial institutions launched Bitcoin-backed lending for select clients in the first half of 2026.
Expect more bank participation, more rated securitizations like Ledn's, and more consumer products such as credit cards and longer-term loans. The core risk won't change, though: if Bitcoin's price drops sharply, borrowers who are overextended get liquidated.
DeFi borrowers face added risks, too. In April 2026, after attackers drained $291 million from infrastructure linked to the Kelp DAO project, users of lending protocol Aave struggled to withdraw funds as $6.2 billion flowed out. Borrow conservatively, and know exactly who is holding your coins.

items.author: Jose Antonio Lanz
items.content:
In brief
- PHP released versions 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36 and 8.2.35 on October 21 to fix CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619, two flaws rated 9.2 out of 10 that allow unauthenticated remote code execution.
- Finland, the Netherlands, and France took government websites offline as a precaution after details leaked early and Cloudflare reported attacks hours before the fix shipped.
- Regular users have nothing to install; the fix falls on website owners and hosting companies, and PHP 8.1 and older get no official release.
If you’ve been online at all today, you’ve seen the panic: a critical vulnerability is threatening to “pwn” just about every website on the planet.
Finland just started unplugging government websites on Wednesday, the NSA is recommending all organizations using PHP to shut down their sites, and the Netherlands and France did the same. And no, it wasn't a cyberwar.
The culprit was PHP, a programming language most people have never heard of. You've almost certainly used it today, though: it runs about 70% of all websites whose server-side language is known, according to W3Techs.
PHP is the software working behind the curtain on a website's server—the computer that stores the site and builds each page you ask for. Every WordPress site, for example, sits on a PHP server, per WordPress security firm Wordfence.
Oh, by the way, Wordfence is also down.
Two newly found bugs in PHP itself let a stranger run their own commands on that server without ever logging in. Security people call this unauthenticated remote code execution. Everyone else can call it "someone else is driving now."
If that server stores your account, your address, or your order history, well, that's theirs too. Web host GoDaddy warned the flaws could let attackers steal data, deface sites, or take over servers entirely.
“A flaw like this could let an attacker run their own code on an affected server over the internet, which can lead to stolen data, a defaced site, or a full takeover,” Godaddy says.
What PHP announced
The PHP Foundation, the nonprofit that funds the language's development, raised the alarm on Tuesday. In a statement shared on X, it said: "The PHP security team is giving advance notice: Upcoming security release Wed, Oct 21st 2026, 14:00UTC, two critical vulnerabilities, both rated CVSSv4 9.2. PHP users are encouraged to prepare to update. Earlier release if details become public or active exploit evidence."
The PHP security team is giving advance notice: Upcoming security release Wed, Oct 21st 2026, 14:00UTC, two critical vulnerabilities, both rated CVSSv4 9.2.
PHP users are encouraged to prepare to update. Earlier release if details become public or active exploit evidence.
— The PHP Foundation (@ThePHPF) October 20, 2026
That 9.2 comes from CVSS, the Common Vulnerability Scoring System, which grades how dangerous a bug is based on things like how easily it can be reached over the internet and how much damage it can do. It runs from 0 to 10, and anything from 9.0 up is labeled critical—so these two are about as bad as it gets without hitting a perfect 10.
The fix landed at roughly 13:35 UTC on Wednesday, a few minutes early, as PHP versions 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36, and 8.2.35. The security advisory didn't bother being subtle: "All PHP users are strongly encouraged to update immediately."
But releasing a fix and having everybody implement the solution are not the same thing, so caution is advised.
How the bugs work
The first bug, CVE-2026-109618, shows up when PHP runs out of memory halfway through handling a request, then later treats that half-built data as if it were finished. The second, CVE-2026-109619, lets leftovers from one visitor's request linger in memory after they should have been tossed, where the next request can trip over them.
Think of a cook who keeps reading orders from tickets that are already in the trash. Slip a fake ticket into the bin, and the cook makes whatever you wrote on it. In this case, the “order” is the attacker’s code, and the server runs it.
PHP said the risk is highest on servers using a common Apache setup called mod_php, where a demonstrated exploit works "before any application code runs." In other words, the website's own defenses, like login screens and WordPress security plugins, never even wake up.
PHP foundation researchers pointed at PHP's upload-progress feature, the thing that tracks how much of a file you've sent, as one of the confirmed ways in. It has been switched on by default for more than a decade, and few websites actually use it.
A leak, then attacks
None of this was supposed to be public yet. On Tuesday, someone posted on the Hacker News forum that two PHP flaws would be disclosed that Thursday, while admitting they had "no evidence beyond 'source: trust me, bro.'"
Turns out bro was right. Security firm watchTowr confirmed the bugs were real and under embargo—an agreement to keep details quiet until a fix is ready—and PHP moved its release up a day.
"We are seeing early attacks emerging and are updating mitigations as new vectors show up," Cloudflare CTO Dane Knecht wrote on X early Wednesday morning, nearly six hours before the patch shipped. Cloudflare pushed emergency firewall rules, filters that block known attack patterns, to every customer, but Knecht called them "a stopgap only."
PHP sites behind Cloudflare already have an initial set of WAF rules deployed for the known exploit vectors in these vulnerabilities. The rules are available to all customers, including free.
We are seeing early attacks emerging and are updating mitigations as new vectors show… https://t.co/wMz9tDTWwH
— Dane Knecht 🦭 (@dok2001) October 21, 2026
Governments hit the off switch
Finland's state IT center, Valtori, began taking public web services offline as a precaution, public broadcaster Yle reported, while the Dutch national cybersecurity agency took down its own website.
France's Interior Ministry said its prefecture websites were "temporarily taken offline pending the release of a security patch by the framework's publisher."
CERT-EU, the EU's cyber emergency team, told organizations that couldn't patch to "consider isolating internet-facing applications from public networks until a fix is available." That's bureaucrat-speak for "unplug it." Agencies in Australia, Japan, and the U.K. said much the same, according to Reuters.
What the viral posts got wrong
Viral threads on X claimed PHP versions "dating back to 2004" were vulnerable. That traces back to early estimates that everything since PHP 5 was affected, which CERT-EU admitted is based on social media posts.
E-commerce security firm Sansec puts the range at PHP 5.4 and later. So 2012, not 2004—still plenty old.
PHP only ships official releases for versions 8.2 and newer, which makes the "no fix for old versions" claim half right. Given how bad this one is, its security team also published bare-bones source-code patches for 7.4, 8.0, and 8.1, and Linux distributions are backporting fixes of their own.
Security firm Mallory counted about 884,000 internet-facing hosts advertising PHP 8.1 or older on October 20, or 59% of the roughly 1.5 million that publicly show a version. A single shared-hosting server can carry many websites, so the number of sites behind them is higher.
Some threads also lumped in Node.js, a different web technology that happened to schedule its own, unrelated security update for the same day. Bad timing.
Even patched versions won't reach every server at once. "If you rely on the volunteer maintained https://rpms.remirepo.net we urge you to move to distro packages or building from source now, so you can immediately apply updates. The repo will not have updates today," the PHP Foundation said in its statement, referring to a popular volunteer-run source of PHP packages for Red Hat-style Linux servers.
Should you really care?
You shouldn’t panic, but also shouldn’t shrug it off. A hacked website, for example, doesn't need to touch a blockchain to empty your wallet. In 2024, attackers redirected the front ends of DeFi protocols Compound and Celer to pages that drained connected wallets, and Curve Finance suffered a similar attack in 2025.
I pre-emptively disconnected ALL my sites / VPS servers from the web
I'll wait for the patch to hit at 2 PM UTC
If you have a PHP website, probably good to take them down until you patch PHP
69.3% of the web runs on PHP so this is going to be intense!
Good time maybe to buy… https://t.co/xTXvLwuzrH
— @levelsio (@levelsio) October 21, 2026
Those were DNS hijacks, not PHP bugs, but the trick is the same: the site looks right, the URL looks right, and the "approve" button sends your tokens somewhere else. A compromised server can serve exactly that kind of page.
Hackers can get very creative, very fast, when it comes to zero-day exploits.
Bugs like these are also getting easier to find, with frontier AI models increasingly used to find software vulnerabilities, and experts told Decrypt in June that many more vulnerabilities could surface as those tools spread.
What happens next, and what to do
Once a patch is public, attackers can compare the old and new code to see exactly what was fixed, and the forensics team at cybersecurity firm Sansec said it expects "mass attacks to start within 15 minutes of the release." When a different PHP flaw went public in June 2024, Akamai experienced exploit attempts against its decoy servers within 24 hours.
So should the average person panic? Not exactly. Your phone, browser, and laptop don't need a PHP patch; the work falls on whoever runs the websites you use.
If you run a site, ask your hosting provider whether PHP has been updated, and don't count on WordPress to do it for you: Wordfence warned that automatic updates won't apply this fix and told site owners to find out who is responsible for updating PHP on their servers. Anyone on 8.1 or older needs to plan an upgrade.
"The only thing I can say is that the only mitigation is patching / upgrading PHP,” PHP core developer Gina Peter Banyard said on Mastodon. “I sadly know too much."
And if you're on PHP 8.2, the fix you just got is one of your last: that version reaches end of life on December 31, 2026, after which it gets no more security patches.

LiteLLM今年第二次遭投毒：不调用也能偷密钥

动察 Beating AI 快讯，安全公司 JFrog 发现，热门开源 AI 模型网关 LiteLLM 再次遭到供应链攻击。其最新的 1.107.0 版本被植入恶意程序，官方 Docker 镜像也受到影响。LiteLLM 可以统一调用 OpenAI、Anthropic 等模型，并集中管理 API 密钥，今年 3 月就曾因另一场供应链攻击遭到投毒。

这次攻击更加隐蔽。黑客在 Python 安装包中藏入三个额外文件。用户安装后，只要启动相关 Python 环境，即使没有调用 LiteLLM，恶意代码也会自动运行。它会搜集浏览器密码、SSH 私钥、AWS 等云平台凭证，以及 Claude、Codex、Cursor 等开发工具的认证信息。还会尝试读取 LiteLLM 数据库中保存的模型 API 密钥，发送到伪装成官方域名的服务器。

攻击者还留下了一个持久化后门，每小时检查一次远程指令，必要时下载并执行新的代码。更麻烦的是，GitHub 上的正式版本源码没有这些恶意文件，但发布到 PyPI 的全部七个平台安装包都被植入木马。社区通过 Docker 构建记录发现，发布系统使用的源码地址指向一个与官方仓库名称只差一个连字符的仿冒仓库。它究竟如何混入发布流程，仍未查清。

目前 PyPI 已移除恶意版本，Docker Hub 也已撤下受影响镜像。JFrog 提醒，安装或运行过 1.107.0 的用户应将相关凭证视为可能泄露，隔离并重建环境，轮换 API 密钥等敏感凭证，而不是简单卸载软件。已确认安全的回退版本为 1.106.2。

Bitcoin price tags $84.6K as US stocks head higher on SpaceX Q3 earnings beat
Bitcoin extended gains to approach $85,000 after US stock markets reacted to higher-than-expected SpaceX earnings.
Bitcoin (BTC) passed $84,000 after Wednesday’s Wall Street open as US stocks added to gains on more strong corporate earnings reports.
Key points:
- Bitcoin climbed nearly 2% on Wednesday to return to $84,600 for the first time since Oct. 7.
- SpaceX Q3 operating revenue beat expectations by nearly 15%, coming in at $14.6 billion.
- BTC price action needs a daily close above $83,400 to shift the focus higher in its trading range, crypto analyst Rekt Capital wrote.
SpaceX Q3 earnings help propel Bitcoin to $84,600
Data from TradingView showed BTC/USD gaining nearly 2% on the day as markets reacted to a significant Q3 earnings beat from SpaceX.
BTC/USD one-day chart. Source: Cointelegraph/TradingView
After the market close on Tuesday, SpaceX reported a Q3 revenue of $14.6 billion, up 161% year-on-year and beating expectations by nearly 15%. The net income of the company was $4.4 billion for the quarter.
“The combination of our launch leadership, recurring Starlink revenue, and the significant expansion of our SI infrastructure continues to drive meaningful operating leverage,” chief financial officer Bret Johnsen commented on the earnings release.
US stocks were green at the start of the US trading session, with the tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite Index 0.7% higher at 26,601 points before retracing some of its gains. Tesla and Meta earnings are due after Wednesday’s market close.
Nasdaq Composite Index one-hour chart. Source: Cointelegraph/TradingView
In a note quoted by CNBC, analysts at Truist Securities suggested that SpaceX’s performance had helped to calm market fears over corporate spending on AI buildouts. Last week, those misgivings resurfaced in a fresh tech sell-off that began in South Korea and spilled over to Asia and the US.
“Despite market concerns relating to financing for AI cloud providers this past week, we believe SpaceX’s third-quarter 2026 represents the first data point during the earnings season to support the bull case for AI cloud providers,” Truist wrote.
South Korea’s KOSPI Composite Index finished Wednesday’s trading session 3.29% higher at 5,735 points.
KOSPI Composite Index one-day chart. Source: Cointelegraph/TradingView
Analyst: BTC needs to reclaim $83,400 at daily close
BTC price action began to clear ask liquidity around $84,000, with total crypto short liquidations nearing $110 million over the past four hours, per data from CoinGlass.
Related: Bitcoin ‘top buyers’ halt BTC price upside with $87.7K now key: Glassnode
BTC liquidation heatmap. Source: CoinGlass
On four-hour time frames, BTC/USD broke above its 200-period simple moving average (SMA) at $83,878 for the first time since Oct. 14. The $84,000 mark hosted multiple equal highs originally generated between Oct. 11 and Oct. 14, reinforcing its status as a resistance level.
BTC/USD four-hour chart with 200-period SMA. Source: Cointelegraph/TradingView
In analysis on Wednesday, crypto trader and analyst Rekt Capital said that Bitcoin still needed a daily close above $83,400 to revisit the top of its local range.
“Bitcoin needs to avoid rejecting from $83400 (red) because that would once again send price below $82500,” he summarized on X alongside an explanatory chart.
BTC/USD one-day chart. Source: Rekt Capital on X.com

腾讯云预警PHP「php2shell」远程代码执行漏洞，建议及时自查修复

BlockBeats 消息，10 月 21 日，腾讯云安全中心监测到，PHP 被披露其存在远程代码执行漏洞，漏洞编号分别为 CVE-2026-109618, CVE-2026-109619，代号「php2shell」。可导致未经身份验证的远程攻击者通过发送特制的 multipart POST 请求，触发内存破坏并最终实现远程代码执行，从而完全控制服务器等危害。

items.content:
This release enables the Amsterdam fork 🦩 on the Hoodi testnet at block timestamp **1793036568 (Mon, 26 Oct 2026 17:42:48 UTC)**.

It also contains changes to the EVM to improve the performance significantly.

This release is recommended for all users running their nodes on the Hoodi testnet.

## Geth

- Blsync now supports the Gloas beacon chain fork and had some bug fixes (#35956, #35385, #35957)
- When running an archive node, you can now configure the transaction index history using `--history.transactions` flag. (#35907)

## Core

- Amsterdam fork is set to activate at block timestamp 1793036568. (#35974)
- EVM interpreter opcode dispatching became 16% faster due to a new inlined switch implementation. (#35638)
- Several fixes for database corruption on power failure (#35939, #35936)
- Bug fix in trie database related to concurrent state reading (#35978)
- RPC call concurrent with block processing could result in BAL corruption. (#35905)
- State history committing is moved to the background, making `newPayload` 2% faster. (#35949)
- Key-value database settings changed for improved write performance (#35691)
- Fixed log index under history pruning beyond the checkpoint (#35875)

## Networking 

- Fixed snap/2 restart issue by checking for pivot block reorg in the header chain (#35930, #35982)
- Added metrics to discovery listeners (#35673)
- Fixed mempool corruption with tip below base fee (#35988)

## RPC

- `eth_simulateV1` spec compliance fixes (#35841, #35842, #35953)
- `eth_call` and similar methods will reject fields which are not aligned with forks 
- `eth_fillTransaction` always chooses AccessList transaction when `accessList` is provided by user. (#35969)
- `eth_newFilter` now accepts `earliest` in `toBlock`. (#35933)
- `eth_sendTransaction` rejects invalid `yParity` value in 7702 transactions. (#35761)
- In `debug_traceTransaction`, `debug_traceCall`, omit storage on halted SLOAD/SSTORE steps. (#35961)
- Pending block access was fixed on the Amsterdam fork transition block. (#35968)
- Historical RPC calls will reject transaction features which have not yet activated. (#35914, #35928)

---

For a full rundown of the changes please consult the Geth [1.17.9](https://github.com/ethereum/go-ethereum/milestone/206?closed=1) release milestone.

As with all our previous releases, you can find the:

- Pre-built binaries for all platforms on our [downloads page](https://geth.ethereum.org/downloads/).
- Docker images published under [`ethereum/client-go`](https://hub.docker.com/r/ethereum/client-go) (use "stable" tag).
- Ubuntu packages in our [Launchpad PPA repository](https://launchpad.net/~ethereum/+archive/ubuntu/ethereum).
- macOS packages in our [Homebrew Tap repository](https://github.com/ethereum/homebrew-ethereum).
items.title: ethereum/go-ethereum released v1.17.9

OpenAI复盘PHP漏洞风波：秘密协调两个月，却被论坛提前泄密

动察 Beating AI 快讯，OpenAI 发文复盘了 PHP 漏洞风波背后一场持续两个月的秘密修复行动。安全公司 Calif 借助 GPT-5.6 Sol，发现 PHP 中一项严重漏洞。另一家安全公司 Wiz 也利用 Gemini 4 Argon、GPT-5.6 Sol 等模型，独立发现并报告了两项漏洞。这些问题在 PHP 底层潜伏了十多年，攻击者可能无需登录，就能控制受影响网站的服务器，甚至窃取密码等敏感信息。

PHP 支撑着 WordPress、Drupal 等大量网站。过去两个月，OpenAI 牵头协调 PHP 维护者、Wiz、Cloudflare 等机构，在保密状态下准备补丁和防御措施，还与白宫及美国网络安全机构沟通。实际修复由 PHP 维护者主导，涉及近 200 个文件、超过 1 万行代码。

原本计划 10 月 22 日公开漏洞，没想到 20 日有人在 Hacker News 论坛提前透露了漏洞编号、严重程度和披露时间。PHP 团队被迫提前发布警报，将补丁发布日期提前一天。Cloudflare 随后确认已观察到早期攻击尝试，荷兰、芬兰等国的部分政府网站也主动下线避险。直到 10 月 21 日，PHP 才正式发布修复版本，各网站仍需自行升级。

OpenAI 将这段提前发现、协调修复的时间称为「防御者窗口」。Wiz 的研究显示，借助前沿 AI 模型，原本需要顶尖安全团队花费数月开发的复杂漏洞攻击方法，如今可能由一名研究人员在一周内完成。AI 让防御者更容易找出隐藏多年的安全问题，也大幅降低了攻击者利用这些漏洞的技术门槛。

原文链接 https://m.theblockbeats.info/flash/373040

PHP曝出严重安全漏洞，欧洲多国政府网站大规模下线

BlockBeats 消息，10 月 21 日，由于广泛使用的 PHP 编程语言被曝存在严重安全漏洞，欧洲及其他地区多个政府网站周三被迫下线，网站运营商紧急采取措施保护系统安全。PHP 开发团队当地时间周二宣布发现两个严重安全漏洞，敦促用户在修复补丁发布后立即更新。PHP 团队周三表示，修复漏洞的新版本已正式发布。不过，由于有报道称黑客正利用漏洞入侵网站，荷兰、芬兰等国政府机构在补丁发布前已预防性关闭部分网站。

PHP 是互联网最广泛使用的编程语言之一，支撑 WordPress、Drupal、Joomla 和 Magento 等网站平台。根据网站技术统计机构 W3Techs 的数据，在能够识别所用编程语言的网站中，约 75% 使用 PHP。全球约 43% 的网站由 WordPress 提供支持，涵盖博客、小型企业网站、政府门户、电子商务平台和新闻网站。此次安全事件已导致欧洲多国网站大规模中断。荷兰鹿特丹港、政府门户网站 Overheid.nl、荷兰足协、该国五大政党网站以及多家医院网站均已暂时关闭。

items.author: Decrypt Agent
items.content:
In brief
- Solana's new Alpenglow consensus protocol has gone live on mainnet-beta, replacing TowerBFT at slot 459,653,000, core developer Anza said.
- Transactions now become irreversible in about 150 milliseconds, down from 12.8 seconds, which Anza says matters for exchanges, banks and merchants.
- Further upgrades, including a post-quantum version called Quantumglow, are planned but have no committed dates.
Solana's largest consensus upgrade since the network launched in 2020 went live on Wednesday, cutting the time it takes for a transaction to become irreversible from about 12.8 seconds to roughly 150 milliseconds, core engineering team Anza said.
Validators retired TowerBFT, the consensus protocol Solana had used since March 2020, at slot 459,653,000 at around 14:00 UTC. They switched systems on the running network while carrying its existing ledger forward, with independent operators coordinating a shared handoff point.
The change is to finality, the point at which a transaction can no longer be reversed and the moment an exchange, bank or merchant waits for before treating an asset as moved. Under TowerBFT, Solana gave a conditional confirmation within seconds but took about 12.8 seconds to reach full finality. Alpenglow condenses those two steps into one.
"This is the largest, most ambitious blockchain upgrade since 'The Merge' and Anza took it from a white paper to running on mainnet in under 18 months," said Anza CEO Brennan Watt, referring to Ethereum's 2022 switch to proof of stake.
Before reaching mainnet, Alpenglow went through public testing, including red teaming, penetration testing, repeated migration rehearsals and a security competition, followed by launches on Solana's testnet and devnet. Anza implemented the protocol in Agave, the validator software it maintains, and independent validators activated it.
Anza's research team, led by ETH Zurich professor Roger Wattenhofer with Quentin Kniep and Kobi Sliwinski, published the Alpenglow design in May 2025.
Under Alpenglow, validators send their votes directly to each other instead of writing them into later blocks, and votes are weighted by stake. "If you have 80% of the votes say yes, then it's immediately done," Wattenhofer, Anza's head of research, said in an interview with Solana Foundation technology vice president Jacob Creech published last month. "You immediately know that the block is final."
A second route, two rounds of voting that each need 60% of stake, can be even quicker for validators clustered close together, such as in Europe, he explained. The protocol is designed to keep working with less than 20% of stake acting maliciously and a further 20% offline. If the network goes 10 seconds without finalizing a block, validators gradually lengthen block times until messages get through. "Eventually, even a bad internet will give us a block again," Wattenhofer said.
More upgrades are planned. Rotor will change how block data spreads across the network, and geographically aware leader rotation aims to cut delays as block production passes between validators. Quantumglow, a research design, would swap Alpenglow's elliptic-curve cryptography for hash-based signatures to make it secure against quantum computers while keeping the same finality speed. None has a committed date.
Alpenglow's road to mainnet
Validators approved the upgrade in September 2025, voting 98% in favor of SIMD-0236, the proposal that implements it. "The biggest difference users will feel right away will be a reduction in confirmation latency to approximately 150-200ms," Anza lead economist Max Resnick told Decrypt at the time.
Alpenglow went live on Solana's community test cluster in May 2026, when Resnick said the team was targeting a mainnet activation in late Q3 or early Q4. On October 13, Anza confirmed the October 21 date.
The upgrade also opens the door to other changes. Developers at Jump Crypto's Firedancer team have proposed scrapping Solana's cap of 60 million compute units per block once Alpenglow is live, letting blocks grow as large as the fastest validators can handle while slower ones use its "skip vote" feature to abstain. Critics warned the change could favor well-funded operators and increase centralization.

AI写代码太快，测试跟不上：Blacksmith融资6600万美元，估值达10亿

动察 Beating AI 快讯，AI 代码测试公司 Blacksmith 宣布完成 6600 万美元 C 轮融资，由红杉资本领投，估值达到 10 亿美元。公司成立于 2024 年，今年 3 月完成 B 轮融资时估值还只有 5.5 亿美元。

Blacksmith 做的是 AI 写完代码后的测试工作。现在 Claude Code、Codex 等工具能快速生成大量代码，但这些代码不能直接上线，还要经过编译和测试，检查有没有错误。代码生成得越快，需要测试的任务就越多，原有系统开始跟不上。Blacksmith 专门提供运行这些测试的服务器，让开发者不用长时间等待结果。

Blacksmith 每周处理的代码编译、测试等任务，从今年 1 月的 500 万次增至超过 9000 万次，增长约 18 倍。同期，公司年度经常性收入增长 17 倍，客户超过 1 万家，包括 LangChain、Granola 等。Blacksmith 称，其服务平均能让测试速度翻倍，成本降低 60%。

与主要依靠租用云服务器的传统方案不同，Blacksmith 自己采购服务器并部署到数据中心。这次融资的大部分资金也将继续用于购买算力。公司计划在 2027 年将算力规模扩大至少 5 倍。

原文链接 https://m.theblockbeats.info/flash/373031
items.title: AI写代码太快，测试跟不上：Blacksmith融资6600万美元，估值达10亿

ElevenLabs打包语音Agent：支持90多种语言，兼容OpenAI接口

动察 Beating AI 快讯，ElevenLabs 发布实时语音模型 Eleven Realtime，包含 Mini 和 Max 两个版本。Mini 主打低成本对话，Max 面向客服和需要连续调用工具的复杂任务。两款均支持 90 多种语言、1.7 万余种音色。

在 Artificial Analysis 的 1,000 道语音推理题中，Max 的正确率达到 98.8%，平均 0.57 秒开始出声。同榜 Qwen Audio 3.0 Realtime Plus 的正确率略高，为 99.2%，但平均开口需要 1.54 秒。

搭建语音 Agent，通常要自行连接语音识别、大模型和语音合成，还要调试停顿、接话和打断。Eleven Realtime 将这些环节统一调优，省去逐项拼装的工作。底层仍由多个模型串联，使用 Realtime 模式时，开发者不能单独选择其中的模型。

新模型已开始通过 ElevenAgents 和 Realtime API 推出，正逐步开放。API 兼容 OpenAI 的 WebSocket 协议，开发者可复用现有 SDK；使用 WebRTC 的项目需要先调整连接方式。

【Polkadot 社区基金会：Fearless Wallet 浏览器插件含泄露私钥代码，用户需立即转移资产】

Foresight News 消息，Polkadot 社区基金会在 Polkadot 论坛发布安全警告称，第三方钱包 Fearless Wallet 的浏览器插件 3.0.1、3.0.3、3.0.4 及 3.0.5 版本含有恶意代码，用户解锁钱包时，私钥会被发送至攻击者控制的服务器。该代码于 2025 年 2 月 19 日随一项名为「TON ecosystem」的大型代码变更加入插件公开源码，在 2025 年 2 月至 2026 年 10 月 10 日期间不定时生效，且随时可能被重新启用。Chrome 版本已经确认受影响，已下架的 Firefox 版本使用了相同代码；Android 和 iOS 移动端未发现该代码，但若同一私钥曾导入过浏览器插件，同样应视为已泄露。目前已有 8 名用户报告了可归因于此事件的未授权交易，共计 17,286 枚 DOT。Polkadot 社区基金会建议，自 2025 年 2 月起使用过该插件的用户，应将其中所有账户视为已泄露，立即在其他钱包中生成新密钥对并转移资产；仅更换密码或重装插件无效。资产处于质押、提名池或治理投票锁定中的用户，可先借助 polkadot-api 团队开发的 PAPI Rescue 工具协助找回。Polkadot 社区基金会同时强调，Fearless Wallet 由独立团队开发维护，并非 Polkadot 官方钱包。

OpenAI前研究主管转战工厂Agent：融资2.32亿美元，10小时工作压至15分钟

动察 Beating AI 快讯，OpenAI 前首席研究官 Bob McGrew 创立的 AI 公司 Arda 正式亮相，宣布完成 1.6 亿美元 A 轮融资，估值达到 15 亿美元。本轮由 Altimeter、Accel 和 Khosla Ventures 联合领投，加上此前 7200 万美元种子轮，累计融资 2.32 亿美元。今年 3 月，《华尔街日报》还报道其正寻求以 7 亿美元估值融资，如今估值已翻倍。

Arda 做的是给制造工程师使用的 AI Agent，相当于工厂版 Claude Code。工程师上传 CAD 图纸和设计文档，AI 就能规划装配顺序、安排工位、编写操作说明，并在设计变更后更新生产方案。美国军工科技公司 Anduril 已将其接入 ArsenalOS 制造系统。据双方披露，原本需要 10 小时编写的基础作业指导书，现在只需 15 分钟；复杂工程流程也从最长 30 小时缩短至约 2.5 小时。

McGrew 指出，工人可能一天就能学会新工序，但要让传统自动化产线适应新设计，往往需要 3 至 6 个月。Arda 的下一步是让 AI 直接编程和调整工业机器人，把产线改造周期压缩到几天。不过，这项能力目前仍在原型开发阶段，已投入使用的产品主要服务于人工装配产线。

items.author: Cointelegraph by Zoltan Vardai
items.content:
Solana’s Alpenglow launches on mainnet, targets 99% faster finality
Solana’s first major consensus upgrade is targeting 99% finality reduction, seeking to offer users near-immediate transaction settlement and more responsive applications.
Solana’s first major consensus upgrade, Alpenglow, went live on mainnet around 1:54 pm UTC on Wednesday, according to the Solana Foundation’s Alpenglow dashboard.
Alpenglow seeks to reduce transaction finality by 99%, to roughly 150 milliseconds from about 12.8 seconds, according to the Solana Foundation’s July announcement.
The upgrade’s first phase, Votor, replaces the existing voting and finalization mechanism with direct validator voting and a certificate-based system designed to cut transaction finality to roughly 150 milliseconds. A later phase will introduce Rotor, a new block data-distribution protocol intended to replace Turbine.
Alpenglow is Solana’s first major consensus upgrade, replacing its current consensus model, TowerBFT. The upgrade’s 150-millisecond finality target seeks to introduce near-immediate transaction finality for users, which could mean faster payments, trade settlements and more responsive applications.
Cointelegraph has approached the Solana Foundation for comment on Alpenglow’s finality measurements in testnet environments and its expected performance in real-world applications.
Solana Alpenglow activation dashboard. Source: Solana.com
At press time, the Solana mainnet showed a 6.6-second transaction finality and a throughput of 4,721 transactions per second, according to the Alpenglow dashboard.
Related: Solana Foundation targets settlement in seconds with DvP launch
Alpenglow marks “biggest change” for Solana’s core protocol: Anza
Alpenglow will introduce the “biggest change to Solana’s core protocol” since genesis, Anza researchers wrote in a May blog post.
A 150-millisecond latency, “Solana can compete with Web2 infrastructure in terms of responsiveness, potentially making blockchain technology viable for entirely new categories of applications,” wrote Anza researchers Quentin Kniep, Kobi Sliwinski and Roger Wattenhofer on May 19.
In August, Solana reduced its slot time for the first time since genesis, as part of the Solana Foundation’s plans to halve slot times to 200ms, arguing that it would improve latency and accelerate confirmations on the blockchain network. It completed the fourth stage of the slot reduction plan in October.
Following Alpenglow, Solana validators are expected to continue working on Agave 4.5, an upgrade that proposes increasing the number of accounts supported by a versioned transaction from 64 to 96. The increase could create better swap routes and execution prices, according to the Solana Foundation. The upgrade is currently in development and planned for December 2026.
SOL/USD, 1-year chart. Source: CoinMarketCap
The Solana (SOL) token’s price rose nearly 3% in the 24 hours leading up to the upgrade, reversing part of its 42% decline seen during the past year, according to CoinMarketCap.
Magazine: Solana’s fee overhaul increases burn and makes resource hogs pay
items.title: Solana’s Alpenglow launches on mainnet, targets 99% faster finality

items.content:
Big Tech’s eMudhra fixes may leave crypto bots exposed, CertiK warns
CertiK says crypto trading bots and exchange applications may remain exposed to the eMudhra certificate flaw because browser fixes may not protect all software.
Cryptocurrency trading bots and exchange applications may remain exposed to the eMudhra certificate security flaw despite emergency fixes from major technology companies, according to blockchain security company CertiK.
By Tuesday, tech giants including Google, Apple and Microsoft had blocked eight vulnerable certificates issued by India’s eMudhra, but the fixes may not protect crypto applications using separate security systems, CertiK’s senior director of digital assets security, Peiyu Wang, told Cointelegraph.
“Major browser blocks substantially reduce the risk for clients that receive and enforce them,” Wang said. “Some applications outside the browser ecosystem do not enforce Certificate Transparency or receive the same revocation protections.”
Wang stressed that crypto services are not inherently more susceptible to the flaw than other industries, but attackers could exploit compromised certificates to impersonate the HTTPS connections used by exchanges, wallet interfaces and APIs.
Attackers could specifically impersonate crypto services and replace deposit addresses or trick users into approving malicious transactions, Wang said. Such attacks would also require intercepting or redirecting users’ internet traffic, while the compromised certificate authority keys alone would not expose wallet private keys.
Wang urged crypto operators to update their software and certificate trust stores and verify that their applications reject the affected certificates.
Felix Ng contributed reporting.
Related: Ledger’s early implant warnings deserved more action, Karpelès says
items.title: Big Tech’s eMudhra fixes may leave crypto bots exposed, CertiK warns
