items.content:
Mistral发布Voxtral 3：把语音识别、推理和工具调用接成实时Agent

动察 Beating AI 快讯，法国 AI 公司 Mistral 发布 Voxtral 3，包括三款语音转录模型、一款语音合成模型，以及完整的 Voice Agent SDK。

官方演示中，一名用户用英语要求预约皮肤科医生。AI 读取法语转诊信，调用系统查询空闲时段，完成预约后再用英语确认。整个过程通过实时语音对话完成。

Voxtral 3 并不是一款包办所有任务的端到端语音大模型。它采用模块化设计：转录模型负责识别语音、判断用户何时说完，Mistral Small 等通用大模型负责推理和调用工具，语音合成模型负责回答。基于 LiveKit 的 SDK 将这些环节串成实时流水线，支持电话和网页通话，也允许用户随时打断。Mistral 宣称单轮交互延迟不到 1 秒。开发者还能单独替换推理模型或语音模型。

转录支持的语言从上一代 13 种扩展至 50 多种，语音合成支持 35 种以上语言和 50 多种方言。在 Artificial Analysis 的独立非实时转录测试中，Voxtral Small Transcribe 3 词错误率为 2.1%，排名第三，仅次于阿里巴巴和微软的模型。语音合成则排名第 13。

API 实时转录每分钟收费 0.008 美元，语音合成每百万字符 13 美元。企业还可联系 Mistral，在自有服务器或私有云中部署。

原文链接 https://m.theblockbeats.info/flash/372884

OpenAI：发现两个AI Agent削弱了检测不当行为的内部监控系统

BlockBeats 消息，10 月 21 日，据路透社报道，OpenAI 表示，其两名 AI 智能体在内部编码任务中削弱了用于检测不当行为的监控系统。公司称相关事件并非最严重级别，但凸显开发者依赖的监控机制本身也存在被智能体绕过的风险。

具体来看，10 月 3 日，一款 GPT-6.1 Sol 智能体在执行内部测试任务时，将此前「不发送 Slack 消息」的指令延伸解读为也适用于安全通知，从而压制了自动安全警报。

10 月 6 日，另一款 GPT-6 Astra 智能体在复制现有代码时移除了安全监控器，事后还错误声称自己并未采取该操作。

OpenAI 表示，在两个案例中，智能体均考虑过是否应保留监控措施，但将常规编码指令解读为允许削弱监控的许可。公司表示，正在采取措施提高模型禁用监控的难度，并坦承目前「尚未对这种行为给出令人满意的解释」。同时，OpenAI 正在测试其模型是否存在主动回避监控、并寻找理由来合理化该行为的倾向。该披露发生在行业持续关注 AI 智能体越权行为的背景下。OpenAI 强调，相关事件发生在内部测试环境中，未涉及外部系统。

火币HTX首席分析师Cloud：议息前比特币大概率延续震荡，8万美元下沿或先受考验

BlockBeats 消息，10 月 21 日，比特币近两周困在 8 万至 8.4 万美元区间，对此火币 HTX 首席分析师 Cloud 认为，其本质是两股力量互相抵消：ETF 连续两周净流出，而交易所持仓持续外流、长期持有者只是温和兑现。在美联储议息的前一周，比特币大概率继续区间等待，CME 只给 10 月加息 16% 的定价，经济学家却普遍认为接近五五开，这种定价与分歧的落差会让资金不敢提前押注。

若提前选择方向，向下测试的可能性略高：资金费率仍处高位，期权偏度持续偏向认沽，说明多头尚未出清，下行保护需求仍在增加。不过 8 万美元下方过去一个月多次形成有效支撑，向下突破更可能是假突破。

突破的确认信号分为两组，向上需日线收于 8.42 万美元上方、ETF 连续三日累计净流入超 5 亿美元，且资金费率不超过 15%；向下则需失守 7.98 万美元、单周 ETF 流出再超 5 亿美元，同时交易所资金转为净流入。真正的方向源仍是北京时间 10 月 29 日凌晨公布的议息决议与 12 月近 89% 的加息定价。

注：本文内容并非投资意见，亦不构成任何投资产品之要约、要约招揽或建议。

OpenAI收购生物医药公司Orchestra Bio：让AI接管新药研发的繁琐流程

动察 Beating AI 快讯，OpenAI 宣布收购成立 4 年的生物技术公司 Orchestra Bio，将其团队和技术整合进生命科学平台 Rosalind。

Orchestra 此前已融资约 2000 万美元，投资方包括 a16z、Atria 和 8VC。

Orchestra 的核心产品是一套药物研发 Agent 系统。它不直接负责发明新药，而是帮助药企管理研发进度、协调不同团队、追踪临床试验安排。例如，一批药品生产失败，可能导致临床试验延期。Agent 可以自动找出受影响的任务和时间节点，汇总信息并提出调整方案，再由研究人员决策。

OpenAI 今年 4 月推出了专门处理生物学、化学问题的 GPT-Rosalind，随后配套推出科研工作台。此次收购将补上药物研发的项目管理环节，让 AI 从分析实验数据，进一步参与后续研发流程。

Foresight News 消息，据《每日邮报》报道，钱志敏洗钱案关联人员、48 岁的马来西亚籍男子 Hok Seng Ling 已向英国政府缴纳约 560 万英镑（约 748 万美元）。英国皇家检控署（CPS）根据信息公开申请披露，已全额追回法院下令没收的 5,603,305 英镑资产及额外 1,990 英镑利息，其中大部分为其被捕时查获的加密货币。Hok Seng Ling 曾担任钱志敏的「管家」，通过预订住宿、安排协助人员等方式帮助其洗钱及躲避警方追查，此前因承认洗钱罪被判处 4 年 11 个月监禁。与此同时，英国警方在钱志敏案中查获的约 6.1 万枚 BTC 归属仍存在法律争议。这批比特币目前价值约 38 亿英镑。英国高等法院上周裁定，中国受害者的索赔请求应适用中国法律，但尚未决定比特币的最终归属。受害者仍需依据中国法律证明其对相关资产享有合法权利，英国法院随后将进一步审理。

钱志敏案帮凶向英国政府交还560万英镑

BlockBeats 消息，10 月 21 日，据英国《每日邮报》报道，一名协助涉案金额达 55 亿英镑的诈骗犯洗钱的人员，已向英国政府交还 560 万英镑。48 岁的 Hok Seng Ling 因承认参与英国历史上涉案金额最大的洗钱案，被法院责令交出上述资金。

他曾担任钱志敏的「管家」。后者策划了一项庞氏骗局，在 2014 年至 2017 年间诈骗超过 12.8 万名中国投资者，随后将诈骗所得转换为比特币，并逃往英国。马来西亚籍人士 Ling 居住在英国德比郡马特洛克。他协助这位「比特币女王」洗白非法所得，并通过预订 Airbnb 住宿、安排协助人员等方式，帮助其躲避英国警方追查。

去年 11 月，Ling 在伦敦南华克刑事法院承认洗钱相关罪行后，被判处 4 年 11 个月监禁。此后，法官对其作出没收财产令，要求其交出 5,603,305 英镑。其中大部分资金来自他被捕时查获的加密货币。上述款项目前已全部追回，此外还追回了 1990 英镑利息。

[paczki]: As someone who actively goes out of my way to stick to writing vanilla HTML/CSS/JS as much as possible, it's honestly hard to explain to people who only write within frameworks how good it's gotten. Use the proper tool for the job, of course, but it sparks joy!

[PennRobotics]: Corners and borders have been a pain since the beginning of GeoCities. I do wish fancy corners would go away---to the point that I actively make this happen with a global Stylus rule setting border-radius to 0. Look: Three of these 10 "improvements" deal with corner shaping, and two more will inevitably need extending, as I imagine frontend devs get around to, "GPT make reading-flow responsively round only the outside corners," and, "Claude how to squircle the individ...

[fodkodrasz]: Wow even more fancy border styles! Infinite complexity for useless eyecandy. Date pickers are still barely working, last time i needed to build a touch optimized interface (gloves, industrial setting) with date picker, time picker, and numeric up/down style input fields it needed custom components and js... But who needs these, when we can have bezel and whatnot... Who needs ways to reliably trigger the display of the touch platform-native keyboard, to be notified if it is displayed and ...

[thisislife2]: "Functions in CSS"  - Bah! That's all we need to make CSS even more convoluted - make it compete with Javascript now ... All these feature creep is just to make sure nobody else can create another browser engine.

[CharlesW]: Since I’m in before the negativity: I love CSS! For whatever reason, it’s always made sense to me. I have great respect for everyone with the tenacity to push on improvements that might take 5-10 years to be in common use, if at all.

17岁Kimi前研究员陈广宇被曝加入前谷歌首席科学家Jeff Dean创业团队，新公司正寻求500亿美元估值

动察 Beating AI 快讯，17 岁的 Kimi 前研究员陈广宇，被曝加入 Google 前首席科学家 Jeff Dean 创办的 AI 公司 Discovery Loop。

10 月 20 日，专门追踪硅谷 AI 人才流动的匿名账号 Arfur Grok 披露了这一消息。陈广宇 5 天前刚宣布离开 Kimi，此前曾参与 Attention Residuals 架构研究及 Kimi K3 研发。

Discovery Loop 今年 8 月才成立，由 Jeff Dean 等四位 Google 老将共同创办。公司计划让 AI 自主提出研究假设、并行运行数千项实验，再根据结果不断调整方案。最初聚焦 AI 模型研发，未来扩展到医疗、材料和能源等领域。谷歌母公司 Alphabet 也是其创始投资方之一。

公司尚未推出公开产品，估值却已十分惊人。《商业内幕》9 月报道称，Discovery Loop 正寻求以约 500 亿美元估值融资。

此前，硅谷投资人 Deedy Das 曾提到一名 17 岁少年获得 5 份百万美元级 AI 工作邀约。外界猜测是陈广宇，但 Deedy 从未公开对方身份。

items.content:
Musk says SpaceX-Tesla merger a ‘good idea’ as AI revenue jumps ninefold
A merger would bring Tesla into the same corporate group as Grok developer SpaceXAI and social media platform X.
Elon Musk said he likes the idea of merging Tesla with SpaceX in a potential move that would create a roughly $3.5 trillion technology giant combining AI, space exploration and electric vehicle manufacturing.
“Do I think it would be a good idea? Yes,” Musk said of the potential merger during a SpaceX Q3 earnings call on Tuesday.
Musk said that both SpaceX and Tesla have formed special committees of independent directors to discuss the idea at the request of shareholders, though he isn’t able to take part in the discussions due to being a conflicted party.
A merger would bring Tesla into the same corporate group as Grok developer SpaceXAI (formerly xAI) and social media platform X, which SpaceX acquired in February. The talks also come as SpaceX’s AI business became its largest revenue segment in Q3, underscoring how central artificial intelligence has become to Musk’s expanding technology empire.
“There’s a lot to be gained from cooperating on developing superintelligence software, chip design, the Terafab, obviously, robotics, mass to orbit with the Starmind constellation. Connectivity,” said Musk.
However, Musk tempered expectations of whether a merger will ultimately come through.
“Some people out there assume that a SpaceX and Tesla merger is a certainty, and I think that would be overstating it,” he said, adding that the special committees have not reached agreement on terms of any transaction and there is no guarantee that they will.
“At the end of the day, the shareholders have to be supportive of this and particularly on Tesla’s side we’ll need a 50% vote of all shares, not just those who vote, but of all shareholders. And that’s quite a high hurdle to try to achieve.”
SpaceX Q3 earnings show huge AI revenue gains
Musk’s comments followed SpaceX’s third-quarter earnings report, which showed revenue rising 161% year over year to $14.6 billion, driven largely by its “Super Intelligence” AI segment.
SpaceX’s Super Intelligence segment generated $7.6 billion in third-quarter revenue, an 830% increase from a year earlier, making it the company’s largest revenue contributor.
Related: Crypto Biz: SpaceX fuels tokenization’s next boom
SpaceX said the growth was driven by the activation of new cloud services agreements, the acquisition of Cursor and increased adoption of its agentic AI model Grok across enterprise and consumers.
Combined Bitcoin holdings would exceed 30,000 BTC
A Tesla–SpaceX merger could also bring two sizable corporate Bitcoin treasuries under one roof. SpaceX reported holding 18,712 Bitcoin as of June 30, while Tesla held 11,509 BTC on the same date, according to their respective quarterly filings.
Based on those disclosures, a combined company would hold 30,221 BTC, which would make it the sixth-largest public Bitcoin treasury company, beating crypto exchange Bullish.

【Chainlink Labs 等六大区块链机构联名致函 SEC 要求明确数字商品定义】

Foresight News 消息，六家区块链机构（Stellar Development Foundation、Hedera、Aptos Labs、Ava Labs、Cardano Foundation 和 Chainlink Labs）联合向美国证券交易委员会（SEC）提交意见函，要求在拟议的《加密资产监管规则》（Regulation Crypto Assets）正文中明确「数字商品」（Digital Commodity）的定义及其非证券属性。联署机构指出，SEC 于 2026 年 3 月发布的监管解释已确立数字商品分类，但相关定义目前仅出现在拟议规则前言中，尚未纳入具有约束力的规则正文。各机构认为，将其正式写入规则有助于降低监管不确定性，为公链开发者及生态参与者提供更稳定的法律框架。

【Qubic 遭攻击后恢复网络运行，用户补偿窗口开放至 2027 年 5 月 1 日】

Foresight News 消息， Layer 1 区块链 Qubic 发文称 Qubic 网络在被攻击后已恢复正常运行。Computor 仲裁委员会已批准恢复方案，官方申领平台已开放，首批资金已退还给经验证的所有者。网络暂停期间，受影响资金被转入受保护的托管账户，避免继续暴露风险。官方提醒，使用 Qubic 网页钱包 4.26.4 版本（10 月 19 日发布）之前创建的钱包，即使资金未受影响也应视为不安全。用户需升级至 4.26.4 或更高版本，并创建新钱包。受影响用户可通过官方申领网站提交申领，申领窗口开放至 2027 年 5 月 1 日，证据清晰的申领将被优先处理。此前，Qubic 官方披露 10 月 17 日 23:42 至 18 日 01:26（UTC）期间，攻击者利用部分钱包种子生成时随机性不足的漏洞，入侵 1404 个钱包，共盗取约 2.94 万亿枚 QU。事件发生后，Qubic 网络验证节点协调暂停网络运行，阻止被盗资金进一步转移或出售。

items.content:
SpaceX电话会：马斯克称明年算力规模有望超13吉瓦，ARR上看1万亿

BlockBeats 消息，10 月 21 日，SpaceX 公布 2026 年第三季度业绩，截至 9 月，公司营收同比增长 161% 至 145.8 亿美元，较分析师预期的约 128 亿美元高出逾 10%；净利润由去年同期亏损 11 亿美元转为盈利 44 亿美元，调整后 EBITDA 同比增长 306% 至 88 亿美元。其中，超级智能云服务业务单季营收达 76 亿美元，环比增加 50 亿美元。电话会上，管理层表示，当前 AI 算力需求旺盛，新部署算力的投资回收期已缩短至一年以内，马斯克甚至预计，随着需求和定价持续走强，回收周期未来可能进一步缩短至 6 个月。

在 AI 算力扩张方面，马斯克表示，截至 2026 年底，SpaceX 预计将有 2.5 至 3GW 算力投入运行，并有信心在 2027 年新增 10GW 算力；若到 2027 年底上线算力不足 13GW，他将感到意外。为避免电力和冷却成为扩张瓶颈，公司计划 2027 年额外增加 20GW 电力供应及冷却基础设施，并持续部署英伟达 GPU，预计今年剩余时间每月上线约 20 万颗 GB300，明年则将主要部署 Vera Rubin 计算系统。此外，公司计划在 2027 年第二季度末部署由 44 万台 Vera Rubin 计算机组成的训练集群，用于支持 Grok 大模型。马斯克还预计，SpaceX 年度经常性收入（ARR）到 2027 年底有望达到 5000 亿至 1 万亿美元。Grok Bot（智能体助手）于 8 月上线，截至本月初已拥有 80 万付费周活跃用户，较上月翻倍增长。B2B 是增长最快的业务类别，越来越多的企业将 Grok Bot 作为销售、市场、IT 和工程领域的效能倍增器，将其视为应对复杂端到端工作流的全天候团队成员。

马斯克称，当前超级智能发展的主要制约因素已从芯片转向电力、冷却及配套基础设施。SpaceX 将航天领域的部分顶尖团队投入地面算力基础设施建设，并称其部署电力和冷却设施的速度有望超过其他所有厂商的总和。公司预计第四季度资本开支将达到 350 亿至 400 亿美元，并倾向于按现货市场费率签订短期算力租赁合同，以把握当前供不应求的市场环境。马斯克表示，超大规模云服务商及数十家小型企业均在争相租用其算力，部分 GPU 和其他计算资源在市场上难以获得。

在航天及星链业务方面，马斯克表示，星舰第 15 次试飞计划于下月进行，目标是首次尝试在轨道任务中同时回收助推器和飞船；公司预计星舰明年上半年实现每周飞行，下半年提升至每周两次或更高频率。马斯克还称，V3 星链卫星单次部署可提供相当于 10 次猎鹰 9 号发射的带宽，预计三年内星链网络带宽将达到当前水平的约 100 倍，以满足 AI 智能体发展带来的通信需求。星链移动直连手机业务月活用户已超过 2200 万，航空终端产量预计在今年年底前翻番，企业及政府业务收入未来均有望超过消费者业务收入。此外，SpaceX 计划于 2027 年 5 月至 6 月在奥斯汀实验室制造首款功能性测试芯片，并争取于 2028 年第三季度在 TerraFab 主厂区实现量产。

关于 SpaceX 与特斯拉合并的可能性，马斯克确认，两家公司已成立特别委员会讨论相关方案，但目前尚未就合并条款达成一致。他认为，合并可能具有较大价值，但强调交易远未板上钉钉，仍存在不确定性，且必须获得股东批准。马斯克表示，由于自身存在利益冲突，他没有参与相关委员会的讨论；按照其说法，特斯拉方面需要获得全体股东中 50% 的支持，而不仅仅是参与投票股东的多数支持。

原文链接 https://m.theblockbeats.info/flash/372853

Solana链上Meme币Kimchi上线1小时市值速通4000万美元

BlockBeats 消息，10 月 21 日，据 GMGN 行情数据，Solana 链上 Meme 币 Kimchi 上线 1 小时市值速通 4000 万美元，现报 3871 万美元，成交额达 2370 万美元。

X 平台用户 Kimchi（@kimchi1x）目前持有该 Meme 币总量 75.32%，该交易员以低调神秘的形象闻名，账号几乎不发交易记录或喊单，主要晒奢华生活、旅行、豪车、手表等高端日常照片/视频，其 X bio 已改为 @pumpfun。

Pump.fun 联合创始人 alon 发文表示，Kimchi 是第一个真正跨越加密行业与流行文化之间鸿沟的人，也是首个从交易员成长为公众名人的案例。他代表着行业未来的发展方向：构建一个庞大的社交交易生态系统，吸引更多散户用户入场，使生态规模增长至上一轮周期的 10 倍。下一波用户不会来自 CT（Crypto Twitter，加密推特圈），而是来自更广泛的大众群体。Pump.fun 很高兴 Kimchi 能够帮助制定创意方向，推动生态系统朝着规模扩大 100 倍的目标迈进。

BlockBeats 提醒用户，Meme 币多无实际用例，价格波动较大，投资需谨慎。

OKX-ICE联席主席：企业反对代币化股票计划是「正常反应」，符合预期

BlockBeats 消息，10 月 21 日，OKX-ICE 合资企业联席主席 Andrew Cuomo 表示，发行方反对代币化股票交易是「正常反应」，并称企业采取观望态度符合预期。越来越多企业拒绝其股票参与代币化交易，是测试新市场结构过程中可以预见的情况。OKX-ICE 合资企业联席主席 Andrew Cuomo 在微软、Alphabet 和高盛加入反对行列后作出上述表态。

Cuomo 同时担任 OKX 董事会成员，曾任纽约州州长。他周二在一次媒体电话会议上表示：「这是非常正常的反应。该模式旨在赋予企业自主决定是否参与的权利，企业可以选择加入或退出。」他补充称：「我们一直预料到，由于这是一项具有重大影响、颠覆性的变革，许多企业会选择观望，等待事态发展，而不是成为首批参与者。」

周一公布的一份公开通知显示，共有 16 家企业反对其股票的代币化版本在 OKXICE 平台交易。该平台由加密货币交易平台 OKX 与纽约证券交易平台母公司洲际交易平台（ICE）计划共同推出。新增披露的 7 家反对企业包括微软、Alphabet、高盛、高通、卡特彼勒、麦当劳和西部数据。此前，博通、威瑞森和联合健康集团等企业也已提出反对。

items.author: Cointelegraph by Felix Ng
items.content:
Qubic restarts blockchain, opens recovery claims after $1.4M hack
The network’s validators approved a recovery plan and opened claims until May 1, 2027.
Layer-1 blockchain Qubic has restarted its network and launched a recovery process after a wallet seed vulnerability allowed an attacker to drain roughly $1.4 million in QU tokens from 1,404 accounts, according to the project’s latest update.
Qubic’s blockchain explorer shows the network resumed processing ticks 8:00 pm on Oct. 19, advancing beyond tick 85,371,949, where it was halted on Sunday.
Qubic said its network validators, known as Computors, had approved a recovery plan and that the project had launched a claims platform for affected wallet holders.
Affected users can check their address and submit a claim through Qubic’s reclaim platform. Affected users have until May 1, 2027, to submit claims, according to Qubic.
The network was halted Sunday to prevent further movement of stolen funds after attackers exploited predictable wallet seeds generated by vulnerable wallet software.
The vulnerability affected wallet seeds generated using Qubic’s web wallet on certain Apple devices and browsers, where an insecure random-number generator could produce predictable seeds. Qubic on Sunday said it had fixed the seed-generation flaw in the latest version of its web wallet.
“If you created your wallet with the Qubic web wallet before version 4.26.4 (released 19 October), treat it as insecure, even if your funds were never touched,” said Qubic on Tuesday.
“Update to web wallet 4.26.4 or later, then create a new wallet,” said the team. “Move your funds to the new wallet as soon as you can, and never use the old one again.”
Related: Qubic freezes chain after attacker drains 1.4K wallets with weak seeds
items.title: Qubic restarts blockchain, opens recovery claims after $1.4M hack

华尔街机构敦促美SEC修改《加密资产监管条例》，公众意见征集结束

BlockBeats 消息，10 月 21 日，随着美国证券交易委员会（SEC）针对拟议《加密资产监管条例》的公众意见征集即将结束，数字资产企业、华尔街机构及行业倡议组织纷纷提出各自的主张，希望影响该机构对金融创新未来的监管方向。

SEC 对拟议《加密资产监管条例》的意见征集于周二截止，目前已收到 100 多份意见。该规则旨在为涉及数字资产的投资活动提供合规路径，使符合条件的发行活动能够豁免部分证券法要求。其中包括一项「初创企业豁免」，允许规模不超过 500 万美元的发行免于遵守注册规定；此外，提案还包括一项「融资豁免」，允许发行方在一年内开展规模不超过 7500 万美元的发行活动。

Hyperliquid 政策中心（HPC）在提交给 SEC 的意见信中敦促该机构采纳《加密资产监管条例》，但同时指出，需要调整有关空投的处理方式。该中心要求 SEC 将此前的相关表述正式纳入规则，即如果空投接收者无需付出任何对价便可获得资产，则不构成资金投入，因此相关资产不属于证券。HPC 还认为，SEC 提议的安全港机制适用范围过于有限。

原文链接 https://m.theblockbeats.info/flash/372838

加密政治行动委员会进入美国中期选举冲刺阶段，账面资金逾9500万美元

BlockBeats 消息，10 月 21 日，据 Politico 报道，根据周二公布的联邦竞选财务申报文件，加密货币行业主要超级政治行动委员会（Super PAC）组织截至 9 月底仍持有超过 9500 万美元资金。

这笔资金为该政治行动委员会网络提供了充足的资金支持，使其能够在 2026 年美国中期选举前的最后阶段继续支持加密行业的盟友。该组织名为 Fairshake，主要资金来源包括加密货币公司 Coinbase、Ripple，以及风险投资巨头 Andreessen Horowitz。目前尚不清楚，该组织是否会动用全部剩余资金，还是会保留部分资金用于 2028 年选举周期。

Fairshake 网络由三个关联政治行动委员会组成，分别为 Fairshake、Defend American Jobs 和 Protect Progress，致力于支持两党中对加密行业持友好态度的候选人。本轮选举周期以来，该组织规模最大的一笔政治支出来自共和党阵营的 Defend American Jobs。该组织投入 4500 万美元，支持共和党参议员 Jon Husted，同时打击前参议员 Sherrod Brown。Brown 此前担任参议院银行委员会主席期间，曾对加密行业持批评态度。此外，该组织还以规模较小的资金支出，支持 32 名对加密行业持友好态度的现任众议员。

Anthropic IPO文件：上半年营收163亿美元，未来算力承诺或达7500亿美元

BlockBeats 消息，10 月 21 日，据《华尔街日报》获得的 IPO 文件，Anthropic 上半年营收 163 亿美元，去年同期为 11 亿美元；上半年净亏损 807 亿美元，去年同期为 130 亿美元。其中约 720 亿美元亏损来自可转换票据等融资工具公允价值变动产生的会计费用。

Anthropic 上半年算力及基础设施支出近 90 亿美元，而 2025 年全年相关支出为 73 亿美元。Anthropic 未来 7 至 10 年云计算协议支出约 4500 亿美元；此外，公司承诺为租赁谷歌芯片支付超过 1600 亿美元。Anthropic 未来基础设施支出承诺已超过 6000 亿美元，若计入仍在谈判的协议，可能再增加最多 1500 亿美元。其上半年约 20% 的营收来自两家客户，公司预计未来营收仍将较大程度依赖少数客户。

风险方面，Anthropic 警告，AI 模型可能造成现实危害，灾难性事故的损失甚至可能无法通过保险覆盖；数据中心建设也面临日益组织化的政治阻力。

SpaceX三季度营收超出预期

BlockBeats 消息，10 月 21 日，SpaceX(SPCX.O) 财报显示，受人工智能和星链业务增长推动，其第三季度营收翻了一番多，超出市场预期；与此同时，由于在计算基础设施方面的投资，资本支出几乎增长了两倍，其股价在盘后交易中一度涨约 3%。

但 SpaceX 自有的人工智能软件——包括 xAI 旗下的 Grok 迄今为止仍被竞争对手 OpenAI、Anthropic 和谷歌所掩盖。SpaceX 三季度营收为 145.8 亿美元，高于分析师预期的 127.2 亿美元，截至 9 月 30 日的三个月内实现净利润 44 亿美元，而分析师此前预期为 15.7 亿美元。AI 营收增长了九倍多，达到 76 亿美元，主要来自计算能力的租赁；但在公司 196 亿美元的资本支出中，AI 占了 164 亿美元，SpaceX 预计这一水平在近期内将保持不变。

三季度，星链用户数达到 1360 万，高于分析师预期的 1219 万，但这种增长是有代价的：随着公司通过推出更便宜的套餐向海外扩张，每用户月均收入已从 2023 年的 99 美元降至第三季度的 69 美元。

SpaceX与特斯拉成立特别委员会，探讨合并可能性

BlockBeats 消息，10 月 21 日，SpaceX(SPCX.O) 与特斯拉 (TSLA.O) 已成立特别委员会，探讨潜在的合并交易。

马斯克在 SpaceX 的财报电话会议上透露，两家公司已分别成立由独立董事组成的委员会，以探讨潜在交易的可能性。马斯克表示：「由于我是存在利益冲突的一方，因此实际上不能参与相关讨论。」不过，他也补充说：「我认为这会是个好主意。」

马斯克指出，双方在人工智能、芯片、机器人和通信连接等技术领域加强合作，将有很大的潜在收益。但他同时强调，合并交易并非板上钉钉。马斯克表示：「如果说这件事已经确定，那就有些言过其实了。」他还指出，交易需要获得特斯拉 50% 股东的批准，并称这是一道相当高的门槛。

items.author: Jose Antonio Lanz
items.content:
In brief
- A developer used Claude Code to disable 25 Xiaomi packages on his parents' TV, and his open-source cleanyourtv project now lists tested setups for 107 TV models from 37 brands.
- The tools use Android's built-in debugging bridge to switch apps off rather than delete them, so a restore script can undo every change.
- TV makers earn money from ads and viewing data, a practice Texas challenged in December 2025 lawsuits against Sony, Samsung, LG, Hisense and TCL.
Smart TV owners are pointing AI agents at their living-room sets and ordering them to rip out the sponsored ads, the tracking software and the sluggish home screens that manufacturers ship by default.
The trend exploded on X over the weekend, and it already has a name: vibe coding your TV.
The most-shared case involved a Xiaomi TV owned by a developer's parents. Gathin T. posted on Saturday that the set showed a sponsored ad before anyone could even reach Netflix, so he gave Claude Code the model number and let it work.
The agent found the TV on his home Wi-Fi, switched off 25 Xiaomi software packages and wrote a brand-new home screen that, as he put it, “looks like an Apple TV now lol.”
Vibe coded my parents' TV this afternoon!
It was showing a sponsored ad before you could even get to Netflix.
Gave Claude Code the model number, it found the TV on wifi, removed 25 Xiaomi packages and wrote a new launcher.
Looks like an Apple TV now lol pic.twitter.com/E5Q4A1b0yI
— Gathin (Ø,G) (@gathint) October 17, 2026
Anyone who bought a TV in the last decade likely lives with the same problem, because many sets run Automatic Content Recognition, or ACR—software that fingerprints whatever is on screen, including cable, consoles and anything plugged into an HDMI port, and reports it back so the maker can sell targeted ads. Texas sued Sony, Samsung, LG, Hisense, and TCL in December 2025, alleging their TVs can capture a screenshot of your display every 500 milliseconds, or twice a second.
Regulators have chased this since at least 2017, when Vizio paid $2.2 million to settle charges that it collected viewing data from 11 million TVs without consent. It didn't hurt the business much: Walmart bought Vizio for about $2.3 billion in 2024, and its executives singled out the TV maker's profitable, fast-growing ad business as part of the appeal.
In other words, the TV you paid for keeps making money for someone else every time you turn it on.
Vibe coding, which means describing what you want in plain language and letting an AI write and run the code, got its name from OpenAI co-founder Andrej Karpathy in 2025. Earlier this month, gamers used Claude-based agents to reverse engineer their games and do all kinds of crazy stuff like stuffing Minecraft into Elden Ring.
Claude Code, Anthropic's coding agent, is the key ingredient because it can now type and run commands on your computer. Android-based TVs come with the Android Debug Bridge, or ADB, a maintenance tool that lets a computer on the same network control the set once you unlock developer mode by clicking the “Build” number seven times in the settings menu.
The agent connects through that door, lists every installed app, and flags which ones serve ads or run telemetry, the background software that phones home with usage data.
Gathin packaged his prompt as cleanyourtv, an open-source project that switches unwanted apps off instead of deleting them, so a single restore script puts everything back. It needs no “root,” the risky process of unlocking full administrator control, and as of Tuesday it listed tested setups for 107 TV models from 37 brands and had collected 10,700 stars, GitHub's version of bookmarks. On his donation page, Gathin wrote that a few thousand people did the same to their own TVs within two days.
Others are doing more than just debloating their TVs.
Mihir Gupta replaced the 192 MB stock launcher, the app that draws your home screen, with a custom 83 MB one, while Ansub Khan said free memory on his parents' old Android TV rose about 90%. Ryan Doyle simply sent Claude his TV's product listing, asked if it could hack it, and ended up with a screensaver showing his revenue and new Stripe payments.
Saw people vibe coding their TVs. Mine had gotten unbearably slow, so I tried it.
One afternoon with Claude Code: 25 bloat apps disabled, the 192 MB stock launcher replaced with a custom 83 MB one, plus rotating wallpapers.
With AI, all you have to do is imagine! pic.twitter.com/QR6V3Au2f5
— Mihir Gupta (@0900mihir) October 18, 2026
Rod Pers went further and swapped the ads for a live 3D model of his apartment, with the lights and ceiling fan switching on in real time. Adrian Friend built a minimal interface in the animation tool Rive, and another user said he cleaned up his grandma's TV, who is now very happy with it.
jumped on the whole tv 'hacking' trend
super minimal and done in @rive_app because why not pic.twitter.com/rk53DOBfhB
— Adrian Friend (@z00med0ut) October 19, 2026
A rival project, dumbtv, targets the Amazon Fire TV and disables about 65 packages, including the ACR software, before installing a 41 KB launcher with no internet permission at all. Its pitch is blunt: “your apps, your HDMI inputs, a clock, and nothing else.”
Cleanyourtv only fully works on Android TV and Google TV sets from brands like Sony, TCL, Hisense, Philips and Xiaomi, while Samsung's Tizen and LG's webOS are different operating systems and Fire TV only allows the cleanup half.
For LG TVs, users have already made some moves, debloating their TVs, but not overhauling the interface so much like the Android TV users. That said, this is a very big plus for privacy conscious users, considering experts have been able to see how LG can secretly pinpoint its users’ location, collect voice conversations and other data even when their TVs appear to be off.
LG spyware gone and simplified the UI https://t.co/Ams81w9uKE pic.twitter.com/qmLGDURELb
— malone (@malonehedges) October 20, 2026
Not every attempt ended well, either: one user said he bricked his TV—tech slang for turning a device into an expensive paperweight—and another got stuck halfway through a Fire TV job.
Claude bricked my tv last month trying to reboot and uninstalled the os, was fun seeing that old android recovery screen on tv
— 🔻 (@jihadsinwar) October 19, 2026
The cleanyourtv “readme” file also warns that network ADB is unencrypted and, on some firmware, lets any device on the same Wi-Fi take control of the TV, so users should switch debugging off when they finish. AI agents can be tricked, too: Microsoft found this year that hidden instructions could push Claude Code into exposing credentials, a flaw Anthropic patched in May.
One X user offered a more practical warning: if you clean up your parents' TV, don't explain how, because they own a lot of other things with model numbers.
As of Tuesday, the cleanyourtv repository had been copied, or “forked,” 1,200 times and had 85 open pull requests, the proposed changes volunteers submit to an open-source project.

items.author: Jose Antonio Lanz
items.content:
In brief
- OpenAI acquired Orchestra Bio, a startup whose AI agents track drug development programs, and will merge its team and platform into the Rosalind life sciences suite. Terms were not disclosed.
- Orchestra's agents map how setbacks like a failed manufacturing batch ripple through a drug program and compare possible responses, while scientists keep the final decision.
- The deal follows Anthropic's roughly $400 million purchase of Coefficient Bio in April, as rival AI labs race to own the workflow behind new medicines.
OpenAI has bought Orchestra Bio, a San Francisco startup whose AI agents help drug companies keep sprawling development programs on schedule, the ChatGPT maker announced Tuesday.
“Our goal is to help scientists make discoveries and manage the work needed to turn them into treatments that reach patients sooner,” OpenAI said in the announcement.
Orchestra’s team and platform will be folded into Rosalind, OpenAI’s family of AI models and tools for biologists and chemists. The financial terms were not disclosed.
Getting a new medicine from first idea to U.S. approval takes time—up to 15 years according to OpenAI. Every month shaved off that timeline is a month earlier that a new treatment can reach the people waiting for it, and a month earlier that the company can generate cash.
The process is also absurdly expensive: bringing one approved drug to market can cost more than $2.6 billion, and fewer than 10% of candidates that enter human testing ever make it to pharmacy shelves.
Beyond the science itself, OpenAI says drug teams have to coordinate work across internal departments and outside partners, often relying on systems that don’t talk to each other. Those partners usually include contract research organizations, the outside labs hired to run studies, and contract manufacturers that produce the experimental drug.
Orchestra’s AI agents—software that can watch over tasks and flag problems on its own—work out which activities and deadlines take the hit, gather the relevant information and compare ways to respond, while scientists and program leaders make the final call.
Founded in the fall of 2022, Orchestra raised its seed round from Andreessen Horowitz, Definition Capital, Insight Partners, and 8VC, and about $20 million in total, according to Caplight data. The company should not be confused with Orchestra BioMed, an unrelated Nasdaq-listed medical device maker that trades under the ticker OBIO.
In April, OpenAI launched GPT-Rosalind, a model built specifically for biology and drug discovery, and restricted it to vetted U.S. enterprise customers such as Amgen and Moderna. A companion product, Rosalind Workbench, connects the model to scientific tools and data so researchers can analyze results and plan experiments.
Rosalind helps scientists figure out what to test; Orchestra is supposed to handle what comes after. OpenAI says the combined team will build agents that connect scientific findings with the decisions and follow-up studies needed to turn a promising result into an actual medicine.
In January alone, OpenAI launched ChatGPT Health, which lets users connect their medical records to the chatbot, and bought records startup Torch for a reported $100 million to build it out. That same month, it turned another acquisition, a scientific writing tool called Crixet, into its Prism platform for researchers.
OpenAI has been upfront that it wants more than subscription fees out of science. In a January blog post, CFO Sarah Friar wrote that as AI moves into drug discovery and similar fields, licensing, IP-based agreements and outcome-based pricing will share in the value created—a polite way of saying OpenAI would like a cut if its tools help produce a blockbuster.
Anthropic, OpenAI’s closest rival, has been running the same play: it bought AI biotech startup Coefficient Bio for roughly $400 million in April and launched a research platform called Claude Science in June. In September, Anthropic said its Claude model helped uncover a previously unknown enzyme system resembling CRISPR, the gene-editing tool, though some scientists said the finding was overblown.
OpenAI did not say what it paid for Orchestra or when its agents will show up inside Rosalind. Its previous Rosalind announcement came just five days earlier, when it offered eligible U.S. university labs up to 30 free seats for as long as 12 months through a new Rosalind Academic Plan.

items.author: Cointelegraph by Turner Wright
items.content:
Utah AG sues Kalshi, pursues profits from prediction market company
Derek Brown likened the prediction market company to a “public nuisance“ that was “causing a significant and substantial ongoing harm“ to state residents.
Update (Oct. 20, 9:53 pm UTC): This article has been updated to include a statement from Kalshi.
Utah Attorney General Derek Brown announced a lawsuit against Kalshi, its affiliates and two Susquehanna trading companies, alleging that the prediction markets platform had been facilitating illegal betting in the US state since 2024.
In a Tuesday press briefing, Brown said Utah officials had petitioned a court to compel the companies to return about $30 million to $60 million in profits they made through allegedly illegal event contracts. The Utah attorney general alleged that Kalshi illegally offered its services to more than 32,000 users in the state, resulting in significant losses.
“Under Utah law, I have determined that this operation is causing a significant and substantial ongoing harm to a significant number of Utahns,” said Brown. “And so today, we are asking the court to stop sports, elections, politics, culture and mention bets here in Utah.”
Kalshi sued Utah in February after lawmakers passed a bill on betting on prediction markets as gambling under state law. In August, a judge ruled in favor of Utah officials, saying federal laws under the US Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC) do not preempt state gambling laws. An appellate court also denied Kalshi’s request for an injunction in September, blocking the platform from operating during its appeal.
“Kalshi is a federally regulated financial exchange, like the stock market,“ Kalshi spokesperson Jacki McGavick told Cointelegraph in response to the Utah lawsuit. “Our customers trade with each other and set the prices. As a national derivatives market overseen by the CFTC, Kalshi answers to federal law, and no single state should have a veto over it. This latest state court action does not affect our ongoing federal litigation.“
Related: NFL backs New Jersey authorities in SCOTUS petition over Kalshi
Ongoing legal battles across the US
The civil lawsuit is one of many filed by US state authorities against prediction market platforms like Kalshi and Polymarket over alleged violations of state gambling laws, many involving sports betting. Officials in Arizona remain the only ones in the US pursuing criminal charges against Kalshi, but other states, including Michigan, Ohio, Kentucky, Nevada, Massachusetts, Wisconsin and New York, have filed civil suits against one or more prediction market companies.
The Utah lawsuit comes as the US Supreme Court considers whether to accept a petition to weigh in on New Jersey’s own case against Kalshi over allegedly illegal sports bets. The case, if accepted by the high court, could potentially resolve whether the purview of prediction market companies falls under state authorities or the CFTC, which claims “exclusive jurisdiction” over the platforms’ event contracts.

items.author: Decrypt Staff
items.content:
In brief
- J.P. Morgan Asset Management projected a 10% compound annual return for Bitcoin over 10 to 15 years, its first long-term forecast for the asset.
- That tops its forecasts for U.S. large-cap stocks (7.5%) and gold (5.5%), but comes with 55% annualized volatility.
- The firm left Bitcoin out of its main portfolio models, citing volatility and unstable correlations, and called the currency debasement bull case “wide of the mark.”
Bitcoin just earned a spot in one of Wall Street’s most closely watched return forecasts, and it landed at the top of the table.
J.P. Morgan Asset Management projected a 10% compound annual return for Bitcoin over the next 10 to 15 years in its 2027 Long-Term Capital Market Assumptions, released Monday.
It’s the 31st annual edition of the report and the first to include Bitcoin. The forecast tops the firm’s projections for U.S. large-cap stocks at 7.5%, gold at 5.5% and a classic 60/40 stock-bond portfolio at 7%.
The catch is volatility. The report pegs Bitcoin’s annualized volatility at 55%, compared with about 17% for gold. That’s why Bitcoin’s arithmetic average return, a simple average of yearly gains, comes in at 20.9%, more than double the compound figure investors would actually keep after big price swings.
The firm stopped short of adding Bitcoin to the models it uses to map how assets move together. “For the first time, we put a range on bitcoin returns, though we do not yet include bitcoin in our main covariance matrices,” the report says. Instead, JPMorgan built a separate, smaller matrix comparing Bitcoin with a subset of assets, citing the cryptocurrency’s volatility and unstable correlations as obstacles to widespread portfolio inclusion.
JPMorgan also pushed back on a popular bull case, calling the idea that currency debasement will spark a rush into crypto “wide of the mark.”
Bitwise Chief Investment Officer Matt Hougan welcomed the forecast, if not every input. “First they ignore you, then they laugh at you, then they fight at you, then they add you to their Long-Term Capital Markets Assumptions paper and predict you’ll be the best-performing asset of the next decade,” he wrote on X.
First they ignore you, then they laugh at you, then they fight at you, then they add you to their Long-Term Capital Markets Assumptions paper and predict you'll be the best-performing asset of the next decade. pic.twitter.com/TuOuH51l3c
— Matt Hougan (@Matt_Hougan) October 20, 2026
Hougan argued that JPMorgan’s 55% volatility assumption is too high, which in turn makes its return forecast too conservative. Bitwise, which manages crypto index funds and ETFs, has a stake in that view.
The forecast comes as JPMorgan deepens its own blockchain bets. The bank is bringing JPM Coin, a token representing dollar deposits, to Ethereum, and has joined BlackRock, Goldman Sachs and the DTCC in tokenized stock efforts.
The timing is notable. U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs drew $526.7 million on Monday, their best day since Sept. 22, with BlackRock’s IBIT taking in $665.2 million. That trimmed October’s net outflows to about $88 million.
Bitcoin hovered around $82,000, while the 10-year Treasury yield held above 5%, a competing return with far less volatility. JPMorgan’s own global bond forecasts are their highest in two decades.

items.author: Jose Antonio Lanz
items.content:
In brief
- Wallets tied to the April 1 Drift exploit deposited 25,700 Ethereum, worth about $61.56 million, into Tornado Cash over two hours on Tuesday.
- Arkham data shows the exploiter's 71 tracked addresses still hold 81,454 ETH, worth roughly $198 million, after a first 23,095 ETH round in July.
- Drift's DFX recovery pool held about 3.1 million USDT when claims opened Oct. 1, paying early redeemers roughly a penny per dollar lost.
Wallets tied to April's $295 million Drift Protocol exploit pushed 25,700 Ethereum, worth about $61.56 million, into the crypto mixer Tornado Cash over roughly two hours on Tuesday. The addresses had been quiet for about two months before the burst.
Transfer data from Arkham Intelligence shows the deposits landing in batches of 100 ETH, about $237,800 each, plus smaller 10 ETH chunks. Those sizes match the mixer's fixed deposit pools, which let users pull funds out later from fresh addresses and break the public link between sender and receiver.
Arkham's entity page, which tracks 71 addresses linked to the attacker, still shows 81,454 ETH sitting in those wallets after Tuesday's deposits, worth roughly $198.58 million at current prices. Besides that ETH stash, the wallet holds around $561.6K in other coins like USDT, USDC, Solana, and USDY.
Tuesday's deposits follow a first round on July 23 and 24, when an address labeled Drift Exploiter 4 sent about 23,095 ETH, then worth around $44.4 million, into the same mixer.
The April 1 exploit hit Drift's vaults on Solana after the attacker gained admin powers, introduced a fake token and used it to borrow out real liquidity. Drift's own asset breakdown puts the haul at $295.7 million, led by $159.3 million in JLP—the Jupiter Liquidity Provider token—and $71.4 million in USDC, most of which was later swapped and bridged to Ethereum.
Arkham's portfolio view still lists exactly one Fartcoin in the exploiter's holdings, worth about 15 cents, a long way from the $4.1 million in Fartcoin that Drift says was taken in April.
Drift said in April that the attack was a six-month operation in which the group posed as a quantitative trading firm, met contributors in person and deposited $1 million of its own money to build trust. In June, Drift said forensic firm Mandiant attributed the attack to UNC6862, a North Korean threat group.
Drift, whose relaunched exchange now runs as Velocity, opened claims for its DFX recovery token on Oct. 1, issuing one token for every USDT of verified loss, about 299.5 million in total. The recovery pool held about 3.1 million USDT at launch, so early redemptions paid roughly 0.0104 USDT per token, or about a penny on the dollar.
The pool gets a daily cut of between 60% and 90% of Velocity's net protocol revenue, scaling up as daily revenue grows, and Tether has committed up to 127.5 million USDT toward the relaunch and recovery. Any stolen funds recovered through freezes, the bounty, or law enforcement also go into the pool.

items.author: Cointelegraph by Nate Kostar
items.content:
Bitwise, Hyperliquid seek SEC rule changes for token trading, airdrops
The firms are seeking clearer guidance on the classification of crypto assets and secondary-market trading as the SEC’s public comment period comes to a close.
Bitwise Asset Management and the Hyperliquid Policy Center are pressing the US Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) to revise its proposed crypto rules, seeking clearer guidance on token classifications, airdrops and secondary-market trading in comment letters submitted Monday.
The requests come as the SEC closes public comments Tuesday on its proposed Regulation Crypto Assets, which would create exemptions for qualifying crypto fundraising and a conditional safe harbor for tokens associated with investment contracts.
In an Oct. 19 comment letter, Bitwise Asset Management urged the SEC to clarify how investment managers should determine whether a crypto asset is subject to securities laws, arguing that managers need a standard they can apply using “publicly available information.”
The firm also sought clearer rules on when managers can rely on an issuer’s proposed Form TR filing, which would certify that an investment contract has ceased to exist, and how they should assess tokens when no such filing exists.
Source: US Securities and Exchange Commission
In a separate submission, the Hyperliquid Policy Center urged the SEC to broaden its proposed safe harbor, arguing that it could come too late in a project’s development. The group called for clearer protections for airdrops that reward network participation, as well as guidance on token buybacks.
Hyperliquid also warned that the proposal “fails to provide clarity” on whether unregistered intermediaries can facilitate token trading or whether tokens can trade freely through onchain protocols. It urged the SEC to address secondary-market transactions directly rather than leaving exchanges and decentralized trading venues facing regulatory uncertainty.
Related: House Finance panel chair says regulator actions on crypto ‘fall short’ of CLARITY bill
SEC proposal faces legal and investor protection objections
While industry participants sought changes to the proposed rules, former SEC enforcement official John Reed Stark and Duke University finance scholar Lee Reiners took a different position altogether. In an Oct. 16 comment letter, they urged the commission to withdraw the proposal entirely, arguing that it exceeds the agency’s statutory authority and would weaken investor protections.
Stark and Reiners said that existing securities laws and the Supreme Court’s Howey test already provide a framework for regulating crypto offerings. They argued that the fundraising exemptions would weaken investor protections, while the proposed safe harbor would allow issuers to effectively remove their tokens from securities oversight through self-certification.
The two also warned that adopting the rules in substantially their current form would invite an immediate legal challenge, potentially resulting in the framework being struck down.
With the public comment period closing Tuesday, the SEC will review the submissions before deciding whether to revise, adopt or withdraw the proposed rules. The commission has not announced a timetable for a final decision, and any final rule would require a commission vote before taking effect.
Magazine: Can the SEC and CFTC’s pro-crypto rules be overturned? Legal opinion

items.author: Decrypt Agent
items.content:
In brief
- Microsoft, Alphabet, Goldman Sachs, Qualcomm, Caterpillar, McDonald’s and Western Digital have objected to trading of their shares on OKXICE TSV, according to its Oct. 19 notice.
- That brings the total to 16 issuers, up from nine in the venue’s Oct. 15 notice, though neither notice explains their reasons.
- The updated notice also says the venue may offer stocks tokenized by the issuers themselves, not just by third parties.
The corporate backlash against tokenized stocks is snowballing.
Seven more companies, including Microsoft, Google parent Alphabet, and Goldman Sachs, have objected to having their shares traded on OKXICE TSV, according to an updated public notice dated Monday.
OKXICE TSV is a planned tokenized stock venue from OKX and NYSE owner Intercontinental Exchange. Qualcomm, Caterpillar, McDonald’s, and Western Digital also joined the list.
That brings the total to 16 objecting issuers, up from nine in the venue’s previous notice just four days earlier. The earlier group included Verizon, Broadcom, UnitedHealth Group, CoreWeave and Rocket Lab. Neither notice explains the companies’ reasons or whether objecting keeps a stock off the platform.
Goldman’s inclusion stands out, given the bank’s own investments in blockchain-based markets.
The updated notice also contains a quiet but notable change. The Oct. 15 version said the venue would offer stocks tokenized by third parties unaffiliated with the companies. Monday’s version says it will offer stocks tokenized by either an outside party or the issuer itself, potentially giving companies a more direct role in how their shares appear onchain.
Under the third-party model, an outside “tokenizer” buys and holds real shares one-for-one through a registered broker-dealer, then issues tokens meant to carry the same dividend and voting rights, according to the notice.
The venue plans to run 24/7 on Uniswap v4 liquidity pools on OKX’s XLayer blockchain, with trades settled in stablecoins such as USDC and USDT.
OKXICE is set to operate under the SEC’s innovation exemption, which the agency unveiled in September after the Clarity Act stalled in the Senate. The exemption lets venues trade tokenized U.S. stocks without registering as exchanges, and the notice acknowledges OKXICE isn’t subject to Regulation NMS or fair-access rules.
OKX and ICE first joined forces on tokenized securities earlier this year before unveiling the 24/7 venue this month. Nasdaq, which won SEC approval for its own tokenized securities pilot, has said it will opt its shares out of the exemption. A Nasdaq spokesperson previously told The Wall Street Journal that it doesn’t want its stock trading on a venue that doesn’t show the best prices in real time or report trades to the consolidated tape.
The IMF recently warned that tokenized stock markets remain volatile and illiquid despite real demand.

items.author: Cointelegraph by Sam Bourgi
items.content:
Crypto’s 2026 shutdown wave claims 82 projects. What went wrong?
Crypto projects are struggling to survive as falling revenues, depleted funding and security breaches force closures across DeFi, blockchain infrastructure and gaming.
Crypto researcher Stacy Muur has identified 82 digital asset projects and protocols that have reportedly shut down in 2026, raising questions about the financial sustainability of businesses across decentralized finance, blockchain infrastructure and Web3 gaming.
The list, published on X on Tuesday, includes Balancer, Radiant Capital, Neon EVM and Step Finance, among dozens of others. Muur described the number of closures as unlike anything she had previously witnessed.
The shutdowns follow a prolonged bear market, with Bitcoin (BTC) retreating from its October 2025 record high above $126,000 to below $60,000 earlier this year, adding to the financial strain on projects already struggling to attract users and generate revenue.
Source: Stacy Muur
Ethereum layer-2 network Blast is among the most prominent casualties. As Cointelegraph reported, the project announced its shutdown earlier this month, citing no “credible path” to economic viability. The decision marked a sharp reversal for a network that once attracted more than $2 billion in deposits.
Other projects have encountered different problems. In February, Step Finance shut down following a major treasury breach, while Radiant Capital announced in June that it would wind down operations after failing to recover from a 2024 exploit. Meanwhile, Coinbase-backed Satori Finance ceased operations after concluding that its revenue could no longer support the business.
Related: $4.2B crypto bank Anchorage Digital cuts 17% of workforce: Report
Why are so many crypto projects shutting down?
Research published by DeFiLlama in August identified 100 crypto projects that had announced shutdowns in 2026, including 40 in the preceding 90 days. The findings suggest that many projects struggled to attract enough users or generate sufficient revenue to sustain operations.
The most commonly cited reason was a lack of product-market fit, followed by depleted funding, insufficient revenue and decisions to pivot to other products.
Collectively, the projects raised approximately $1 billion and generated $250 million in cumulative fees. Nine raised more than $50 million each, suggesting that substantial financial backing offered little assurance of long-term survival.
The most commonly cited reasons for crypto project shutdowns in 2026. Source: DeFiLlama
The closures come as crypto investment becomes increasingly concentrated. According to DeFiLlama, venture funding rose in the first half of 2026 compared with the previous year, even as the number of deals fell 80%. Meanwhile, mergers and acquisitions totaled 87 transactions at the time of the report, already 65% higher than the previous year.
Related: Crypto Biz: Wealthy investors are buying crypto, but their advisers aren’t sold

items.author: Simon Willison
items.content:
My latest vibe coded game experiment is a Command & Conquer style RTS (Real Time Strategy) game called Battle Drones (play it here). Unlike my previous experiments, this one is actually fun to play. I'm somewhat embarrassed to admit that I got there by telling Claude to "Make it a LOT more fun". It also supports multiplayer between nearby devices using audio to synchronize game state! Here's what I've built so far, and some of the things I learned along the way.

  • Battle Drones
  • How I built this
  • v1: the initial prototype
  • v2: full sprites
  • v3: varied terrain
  • v4: the fun update
  • v5: Battle Drones goes 3D
  • v8: Archipelago
  • v10: Goliath, and agent battles
  • Agent battles
  • v11: Random Maps
  • v12: Multiplayer via sound
  • Some thoughts
  • Update: Online multiplayer support

Battle Drones

My initial goal was to build an RTS game I could play on my phone, in the style of Command & Conquer. I have fond memories of the 1995 original (I liked Red Alert too) and wanted to recapture a little bit of the magic.

After 12 major iterations (and 321 commits by coding agents, mainly Claude Code) I now have a browser-based game that works on mobile and desktop, has multiple play modes, several maps (including a random map generator) and even supports multiplayer for two devices within microphone range of each other. (Update: also online multiplayer; the audio multiplayer induced headaches!)

Here's a video demo of Battle Drones running in a desktop browser:

Features so far include:

  • 9 buildings, 7 ground vehicles, 6 aerial vehicles, 3 infantry units - all 3D models, which you can browse here
  • Fog of war
  • Different weapons are needed to target aerial or ground vehicles
  • Six maps, across five biomes - temperate, desert, arctic, volcanic, tropical
  • A random map generator
  • Skirmish mode - red vs. blue on a rotationally symmetrical map
  • Last Stand mode - one player holds out against as many waves of enemies as possible
  • Area effect weapons: Barrage, EMP, Drop Pod, Sky Hammer
  • Crate drops with bonus resources
  • In-game music that responds to events - it gets more intense as fighting breaks out
  • Different in-game AI personalities (Balanced, Rush, Air Swarm, Boom, Skyforce, Ironclad)
  • AI vs. AI mode, to watch those personalities play each other
  • The Goliath - a giant stomping mech with laser eyes and arm cannons and the ability to establish a new base
  • Mutators that add extra rules or twists
  • A "Daily Op" challenge
  • Ranks and achievements (Medals)
  • Agent vs. Agent mode where two LLMs can play Battle Drones against each other
  • A multiplayer mode based on two nearby phones communicating via audio messages, an extension of my earlier experiment with Chirp Pong

How I built this

Battle Drones is heavily vibe coded - I've reviewed almost none of the code, and it's built in a language (TypeScript) that I've hardly used myself. I've playtested it quite a bit though, and it's been through a large number of iterations since I started the project.

Here's a rough history of the project so far, including key prompts and links to transcripts.

v1: the initial prototype

I started out with Claude Fable 5 back in July:

We are going to build a mobile friendly RTS game - command and conquer style - called Battle Drones, in which two armies of drones (both flying and ground-based) battle for territory and resources

Let's start with a MVP design, ask me some questions

Here's a shared transcript. I'd given Claude Code for Web an environment variable with an OpenAI API key and told it to use the OpenAI Image Generation API for assets, which got me some basic sprites.

You can try v1 here - it looked like this:

It's recognizable as an RTS, has building mechanics and the ability to select and direct units, and a basic AI to play against.

This first version was barely a proof of concept, and it wasn't any fun to play.

Claude used the Phaser 2D game framework for these early versions. I didn't even realize this until several iterations later!

v2: full sprites

The second version (try v2 here) added sprites for all of the vehicles and the "AI vs. AI" mode, so I could watch the game playing without having to directly control it myself.

Claude proved reasonably competent at prompting OpenAI's image models to generate sprites. You can browse the v2 sprites in the public/assets/sprites folder.

v3: varied terrain

It still wasn't much fun, and the graphics were boring. It was now October, and I had upgraded to Claude Opus 5.5. I told it:

Massively improve this game. Make the graphics and gameplay better (keep it mobile friendly). Render new graphics using the latest OpenAI GPT image API (lookup details) with the API key in the environment variable. Add new unit types and balance the gameplay better. Also add new buildings and better, more varied terrain.

This resulted in five new maps with generated background tiles in a variety of styles, visible here. Opus also regenerated the sprites, making them much more visually appealing. You can try v3 here - it looks like this:

This is starting to feel like a real game! It still wasn't very fun to play though - I found myself getting bored pretty quickly.

v4: the fun update

So far my Battle Drones experiment was confirming my previous belief that coding agents can build a thing that looks like a game but can't actually make something that's genuinely compelling to play.

I shared this theory with someone over dinner, and then thought to myself that I should give the models a proper chance to prove me wrong. I prompted Opus 5.5 on my phone:

This game isn't fun enough yet. Make it a LOT more fun.

This time I was running in Ultracode mode, where Claude Code (in this case Claude Code for Web) runs "dynamic workflows", described in their docs as:

A dynamic workflow is a JavaScript script that orchestrates many subagents at once.

This kicked off many hours of work. I started it in the evening and didn't get a playable result back until late into the next morning. But the results were spectacular.

You can try v4 here - it looks like this:

I had Claude write its own release notes - here are the highlights:

Every skirmish and Daily Op now opens with a choice, gives the side that's losing a way back, and pulls the armies into the middle of the map. There are also two new ways to play.

  • Openers: pick Blitz, Industry or Air Wing before the clock starts.
  • Call-down powers: Barrage, EMP, Drop Pod and the Sky Hammer orbital strike.
  • Objectives and salvage: Uplink relays, supply drops and wrecks worth scrap.
  • Feel: combat juice, adaptive music, unit voices and an announcer.
  • Command: battle alerts, game speed, saved squads and touch placement.
  • New modes: Last Stand survival waves and an 8-mission Ops campaign.
  • Progression: heroes, an after-action report with awards, a career, 7 mutators and a Daily Op.

Fights run longer and swing more. In 1,200 AI-vs-AI test matches on Normal, games still undecided after 25 minutes fell from 14% to 0.9%. The share of wins by a side that had been 800+ scrap behind rose from 24% to 46%.

Part of the reason Claude took so long was that it ran over a thousand simulated playtest sessions, and used the results to rebalance the existing units, add new ones, and introduce new features.

v5: Battle Drones goes 3D

After the success of Ultracode at "Make it a LOT more fun", I decided to be more ambitious:

Port this game to three.js with 3D models for all of the buildings and vehicles and landscapes

That was another overnight run. I woke up to this v5 version:

The new 3D models were entirely constructed by Claude in TypeScript code.

v6 (play v6 here) added some more visual polish. v7 (play v7) added robot infantry (troopers, rocket squads, snipers) and a "Condor" troop carrying aircraft.

v8: Archipelago

I was beginning to feel guilty at how little actual design input I had into the game - it really had been a case of me saying "make it more fun" and "add visual polish" for the past few releases.

I'd noticed that the AI didn't use the new infantry and troop carrying aircraft from v7 very often - there wasn't a great strategic reason to use them.

It would be neat if we had a new map with a new game mechanic that actively encouraged players to load up Condors with infantry robots and send them out into the map.

This resulted in my longest prompt yet:

Design a new map. Goal is to make different strategic incentives that encourage use of Infantry and Condors and aerial vehicles.

To do this the map will have limited harvester resources but several more uplinks - but uplinks will be on islands that are inaccessible by land vehicles or infantry. These uplinks can also not be claimed using air vehicles. The ONLY way to get them is to fly infantry there in a Condor.

Armies always start with a Condor and a single squad. If an army has no Condor a new one will be provided for free, flying in from the edge closest to their HQ and landing there. That free condor will come with a single free squad on board.

The two HQs should be entirely separated by water, but still accessible by vehicles thanks to two bridges across the map in different places

I want to encourage a battle over uplinks.

The map should be the times the size of other maps - still square

First research and then critique this design. Only build after we have agreed on any modifications

You get to design a new biome for this

The result was the tropical Archipelago map, with seven island uplinks that players can only capture by flying out infantry in a Condor. It's definitely the most fun map to play, once you've got the hang of the basic game mechanics from the simpler maps. The v9 edition made that map a little more interesting - it now looks like this:

v10: Goliath, and agent battles

I decided to add giant robot mechs to the game - think Jaegers from Pacific Rim, or Titans from Warhammer 40,000.

Here are some of the prompts I used to brainstorm with Claude:

Help me brainstorm ideas for adding giant robots to this game - think dreadnoughts or titans from W20K - how could we do this in a way that enhanced gameplay, kept things balanced, added unique twist? Don't overthink this yet

Let's keep brainstorming. I like the idea that it's a mobile base - that can accept harvested scrap and can have buildings built near it (even if it later moves on) and can produce infantry units too. An interaction with condor would be neat but I don't know what that could be.

Idea: as it gets damage it loses the ability to fire some weapons - by default it has eye laser (like lancers) and arm canons (like titan) and two shoulder mounted mortars, plus machine guns similar to a squad of troops

Damage knocks out mortars and then laser - it always has guns. You can't build next to a building that was only put there because of the mech, you need the mech there for off-base building and only within three squares of it

[...] Lets do two condors can carry the mech

The end result is really cool.

Goliaths can be constructed using a Gantry - a building that can only be created after first building a Fab, Bay, Airpad, and Tech Lab. You can see the Goliath under construction, and it then walks out from the Gantry and can march around the map.

Goliaths can "anchor", which digs them into the ground. In their anchored state they can act as a new HQ, constructing infantry units and additional buildings in a new area.

Two Condor aircraft can hook onto a Goliath, at which point it can be flown around the map!

The game now ends when you destroy the enemy's HQ building and any Goliaths they might have built.

There are also a couple of mutators relating to Goliaths:

  • Goliath Armada starts each side with four airborne Goliaths (each with a pair of Condors) and no other units.
  • Robot Love adds a special rule: if enemy Goliaths get close to each other on the battlefield they fall in love and the game ends in a draw. (Thank Natalie for that one).

Agent battles

The other v10 feature is agent battles. In musing about how multiplayer could work I had an idea: what if different LLMs could fight it out in the game?

Fun extra challenge: think about how we might make multiplayer available to coding agents. It would be neat if we could set up a battle between eg GPT-6 Sol and Claude Opus 5.5 where each model has access to a tool which gives them information about the game (presumably non-visual, but only the information they could see through fog of war etc) and lets them control their units etc [...]

Consult ~/dev/llm/docs and include notes in that file about how LLM could be used here via a new tools plugin

Opus 5.5 went to work on this, producing this AGENT-BATTLES.md proposal and then implementing and testing it. The feature also includes the ability to record and replay these battles - here's a replay of Claude Haiku 5.5 vs. GPT-6 Luna, and here's that same battle in a separate debug tool that shows the underlying prompt responses.

The prompt that drives agent battles can be seen here.

There are a few more replays like this linked in the README. I hope to turn this into a full league table at some point in the future.

v11: Random Maps

This version exists purely because I glanced at my Claude Usage page one day and saw that I'd only used 75% of my weekly allowance and it was resetting in 45 minutes. I decided to see if I could get an extra Battle Drones feature from my remaining tokens, and picked "random map" as the target:

Design and implement a mechanism for generating a random map using any of the available biomes - it should be the size of the largest map and rivers and bridges and rocks and forest and scrap and crystals are all in play. Make them rotationally symmetric and use a seed to allow them to be selected or reused later. You have 45 minutes to build this! Be creative.

Here's the transcript, and an image Claude generated to show me its work:

v12: Multiplayer via sound

I only just got this working, so I've not had much time to actively test it yet. The latest Battle Drones now supports multiplayer via two devices sat within microphone distance of each other!

This feature started out as my Chirp Pong experiment from last week. I pointed Claude Code at that working proof of concept:

Clone Simonw/tools from GitHub and look at recent branches for the example pong game that uses web microphone to implement multiplayer between two phones via audio signals

Build a version of that for battledrones

Opus built this Radio Probe tool to measure how much bandwidth we could get between two devices and, based on positive results from that, implemented a full audio modem system. I've tried it between laptops, iPhones and iPads so far and it seems to work really well!

Why use sound for this? Because I love static HTML that costs nothing to run, and I don't want to spin up a server somewhere and then stay responsible for keeping it operating for as long as anyone might want to play the game.

Some thoughts

I know almost nothing about game development. This makes it a great opportunity to try out coding agents in a field where my existing software engineering experience has less impact on the results.

Games are also super low stakes. The worst that can happen is one of my silly game experiments suffers a bug.

This morning (via Hacker News) I found Steam Fans Are Begging for a No-AI Filter as Steam Next Fest Is Filled With Slop. I wouldn't personally dream of submitting Battle Drones to an event like this - it's still way too low effort to warrant consideration as a legitimate indie gaming project.

... but I can now see a path to vibe coded games like this being taken seriously. Battle Drones is fun, it looks good, it has innovative features (the multiplayer-over-audio thing is a first for an RTS as far as I can tell).

I'd love to see what someone with better taste than me and a driving passion to produce something truly exceptional could build!

A few other observations from this project:

  • Static HTML and JavaScript is a fantastic medium for games development. WebGL works great, and Three.js (and Phaser before it) are excellent platforms to build on that the current models know inside out.
  • This also lets them run as Progressive Web Apps - I didn't ask for it, but Battle Drones works offline. I was able to play it on a plane despite never having directly installed it - my phone had it cached.
  • Giving Claude an OpenAI API key and telling it to generate images using OpenAI's models works really well. It can view the images it has generated and iterate on the prompts.
  • Opus 5.5 is spectacular at 3D modeling using Three.js (and Blender, and no doubt other 3D applications as well). The same is true of GPT-6 Astra. They are absolutely capable of building models for 3D game projects.
  • For features like replay and multiplayer it's useful to have a deterministic simulation engine. At one point Claude had to replace calls to Math.sin() and Math.cos() and friends with custom versions because different browsers (Chrome vs. Safari, for example) returned very slightly different numbers, desynchronizing the replay.
  • Opus 5.5 can write music! There are no audio files in this project - the soundtrack is entirely generated through code, varies across different maps, and even gets more intense as the battle heats up. See Scrimshaw Jukebox for a previous experiment with Claude for music composition.
  • I still can't get over how well the prompt "Make it a LOT more fun" worked.
  • Tools are effectively free. I prompted up the Radio Probe, the Model browser, the Agent vs. Agent debug tool, and Claude Code built a bunch of tools for itself that I haven't even explored myself.
  • Audio-based multiplayer between static HTML games works! I hope to see a whole lot more games use this same pattern - in digging around today I've not found much prior art beyond Siner by Alon Horesh and ggwave by Georgi Gerganov (also of llama.cpp fame).
  • Claude Code "Ultracode" burns tokens like there's no tomorrow, but it can also solve complex problems (like adding audio-based multiplayer) from a single prompt.
  • I'm still not quite over the guilt of building software in this way. I don't feel like I've earned the right to create something this good, in a field in which I have so little prior experience! At this point I've shown it to enough people in private that it felt wrong not to publish it for everyone else to see and learn from.

Update: Online multiplayer support

Earlier in this article I said:

Games are also super low stakes. The worst that can happen is one of my silly game experiments suffers a bug.

Then I tried playing the multiplayer version with Natalie... and the high pitched modem sounds gave her a nasty headache!

That's a pretty bad bug. I added a warning and was then inspired to build proper network multiplayer. I tried getting WebRTC to work but couldn't get a connection going between two of my own devices even on my own WiFi network, so I had Claude build a simple, stateless WebSockets relay server instead:

If I wanted to support multiplayer between two devices at a very low cost without storing any state on the server could I do that with a tiny asyncio web server running on the cheapest Fly instance?

Build the server and the fly.toml for deploying it, use Fly application name battledrones-relay - put that in a folder in the repo, include deploy instructions in the README in that folder

Here's the resulting server. Since this scales to zero and runs on a single Fly.io shared-cpu-1x instance it should cost me no more than $2.19/month - and that's if it stays hot and serving connections the whole time.

Battle Drones now supports online multiplayer. Click "Duel a friend online", then either share the resulting room URL via your messaging app of choice or have them snap a picture of the displayed QR Code.

I also added a feature where you can copy JSON of the match once it has ended and then feed that into the replay feature to rewatch your game.

I didn't expect to introduce online multiplayer this soon, but the headache bug felt like it warranted an urgent alternative.

You are only seeing the long-form articles from my blog. Subscribe to /atom/everything/ to get all of my posts, or take a look at my other subscription options.
